scenario: 45 分钟面试要设计 ChatGPT：200M DAU、120k 并发流，时间只够覆盖最核心的对话路径。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes to design ChatGPT at 200M DAU and 120k concurrent streams, so scope has to stay on the core chat path.
q: ChatGPT 设计题的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are the core functional requirements for the ChatGPT design? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 发送自然语言 prompt 并收到 AI 回复
查看历史聊天并带着上下文继续对话
编辑或分叉已有消息
跨聊天全文搜索历史记录
why: 本题只覆盖文本对话和历史续聊；编辑、分叉、全文搜索、多模态、工具调用都被放到范围外。先收紧范围，才能把时间花在流式返回、GPU 调度和成本控制上。
why_en: The scoped product requirements are sending text prompts and resuming saved chats with prior context, while editing, branching, search, tools, and multimodal features are out of scope.
options_en: Send a natural-language prompt and get an AI reply.
View past chats and resume them with prior context.
Edit or branch existing messages.
Full-text search across chat history.
optionExplanations: 这是本题唯一必须支持的核心交互：用户发 prompt，模型必须给出回复。
同样在范围内：用户要能回到旧对话并带着上文继续问，否则每次都要重新给背景。
很多人以为编辑/分叉是基础功能，但本题明确把它放在 below the line，不用现在设计。
全文搜索听起来常见，但同样被划出范围，不是这道题要交付的能力。
optionExplanations_en: This is the one interaction the design must support: the user sends a prompt and gets a reply back.
Also in scope: users must be able to reopen an old chat and keep chatting with its prior context loaded.
Editing or branching feels core, but the prompt scopes it out — it is not part of this design.
Full-text search sounds standard, but it is explicitly out of scope here too.

scenario: ChatGPT 设计题只有 45 分钟，深挖预算要留给流式返回和 GPU 调度，其余议题先划到线下。
scenario_en: With only 45 minutes, the deep-dive budget goes to streaming and GPU scheduling, so everything else gets pushed below the line.
q: 哪些内容在本题里明确 below the line？（多选）
q_en: What is explicitly below the line for this design? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 保存最终 assistant message
逐 token 持久化每个流式 chunk
鉴权、滥用治理和内容审核细节
GDPR、数据驻留、隐私合规
why: 系统只需要持久化最终回复，不要求每个 token 都成为 durable record；安全、合规、监控等也不是主线。这样深挖可以集中在 serving 系统本身。
why_en: Per-token durability, moderation, compliance, and operations are scoped out so the design can focus on low-latency serving and GPU capacity.
options_en: Persist only the final assistant message.
Persist every streamed token chunk individually.
Authentication, abuse prevention, and moderation details.
GDPR, data residency, and privacy compliance.
optionExplanations: 保存最终消息其实是本题范围内的基本要求，不属于 below the line，别把它和逐 token 持久化搞混。
确实被划出范围：不需要把每个流式 chunk 都变成 durable 记录，只保留最终回复即可。
同样在范围外：鉴权和内容审核有专门系统负责，这道题不用深挖它们的实现细节。
合规相关的 GDPR、数据驻留也被划出范围，留给专门团队处理，不是这次设计的重点。
optionExplanations_en: Saving the final message is actually in scope, not below the line — don't confuse it with per-token persistence.
This is genuinely out of scope: you don't need to make every streamed chunk a durable record, only the final reply.
Also out of scope: auth and moderation live in their own systems, so this design doesn't need to detail them.
GDPR and data residency are compliance concerns handled elsewhere, not part of this design's scope.

q: 这个规模量级最直接支持下面哪个设计判断？
q_en: Which design call does this scale estimate support most directly?
options: GPU 调度和利用率必须被认真设计
并发流不多，同步阻塞调用完全够用
单实例 Postgres 就能撑住所有读写流量
这个规模下不需要考虑排队或降级
why: 200M DAU、约 20k prompts/sec 峰值、120k 并发流意味着 GPU 调度和利用率才是这题的核心难点，而不是常规 CRUD 扩展。
why_en: At roughly 200 million daily users and 120 thousand concurrent streams, GPU scheduling and utilization become the central design problem, not ordinary CRUD scaling.
scenario: 设计题设定 ChatGPT 服务约 200M DAU、峰值约 20k prompts/sec、约 120k 并发生成流。
scenario_en: The ChatGPT service is scoped at about 200M DAU, a peak of about 20k prompts per second, and about 120k concurrent generation streams.
options_en: GPU scheduling and cross-request utilization need serious design, this is not ordinary CRUD scale.
Concurrency is low enough that synchronous blocking calls are fine.
A single Postgres instance can handle all read/write traffic.
At this scale there is no need to think about queuing or degradation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数，衡量每天有多少用户使用产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU is the number of unique users active on a given day.

optionExplanations: 200M DAU、120k 并发流让 GPU 才是稀缺资源，调度和利用率必须认真设计，这是本题的核心难点。
把 120k 并发流当成“不多”是低估了并发；同步阻塞调用在这个量级下会直接堵死请求。
Postgres 单实例能扛住聊天记录这种简单行存储，但这题的瓶颈根本不在数据库读写。
排队和降级恰恰是这个量级最需要的机制，跳过它们会让高峰期请求无限堆积。
optionExplanations_en: At 200M DAU and 120k concurrent streams, GPUs are the scarce resource, so scheduling and utilization need real design work.
Calling 120k concurrent streams 'low' underestimates it — synchronous blocking calls would stall requests at this scale.
A single Postgres instance can handle the simple chat rows fine, but that's not where this problem's bottleneck lives.
Queuing and degradation are exactly what this scale needs — skipping them lets peak traffic pile up without bound.

q: 本题最关键的用户感知延迟指标是什么？
q_en: Which user-visible latency metric matters most in this design?
options: 后端数据库写入路径的 p99 延迟表现
首 token 延迟（TTFT）低于约 500ms
完整回复内容必须整体在 2 秒内结束
模型离线训练阶段的吞吐量统计指标
why: 用户按下回车后最怕看到空白，所以 TTFT 比完整生成耗时更影响体验；完整回复仍可持续到约 30 秒。
why_en: Time to first token under roughly 500 milliseconds matters more than total completion time because a blank screen feels broken.
scenario: 用户敲回车后期待立刻看到反应；产品目标是让首个 token 尽快出现，完整回复允许持续到约 30 秒。
scenario_en: After the user presses Enter, the product should show a first token quickly; the full answer may keep streaming for about 30 seconds.
options_en: Backend database write-path p99 latency performance.
Time to first token (TTFT) under about 500ms.
The entire response content must finish within 2 seconds.
Offline model-training throughput statistics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从发送请求到第一枚 token 出现的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTFT is the time from sending a request to the first token appearing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求都能在这个时间内完成的延迟阈值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the threshold that 99 percent of requests complete within.

optionExplanations: 数据库写入 p99 延迟确实重要，但用户看到的是首屏反应，不是后端写入耗时。
TTFT 直接对应用户按下回车后多久看到第一个字，是本题真正要保的体验指标。
把整体回复压到 2 秒不现实——30 秒生成期是产品允许的，卡住的只是首字。
训练吞吐量属于离线阶段的指标，跟用户此刻等待的在线体验完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: DB write p99 is a real metric, but it's not what the user perceives right after hitting Enter.
TTFT is exactly how long the user waits to see the first character, the experience this design must protect.
Forcing the whole reply under 2 seconds is unrealistic — a 30-second generation window is allowed, only the first token can't lag.
Training throughput is an offline metric, unrelated to what a user experiences during a live request.

q: 对 conversation state，应该选择哪种 CAP 倾向？
q_en: Which CAP bias should conversation state use?
options: 强一致优先，宁可整体阻塞
完全不持久化聊天状态
可用性优先，接受短暂状态不一致或降级
所有地区同步提交后才响应
why: 聊天状态不是股票交易这类强一致场景，短暂降级或返回错误比让整个系统等完美同步更好。目标是约 99.9%+ 可用性。
why_en: Conversation state favors availability over strong consistency because temporary degradation is preferable to blocking the whole system.
tradeoff: 可用性 vs 强一致性（CAP）
options_en: Prioritize strong consistency, even if it blocks the whole system.
Do not persist conversation state at all.
Prioritize availability and accept brief state inconsistency or degradation.
Only respond after every region commits synchronously.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性、可用性、分区容忍性三者在网络分区下不可兼得的经典权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP describes the trade-off among consistency, availability, and partition tolerance during a network partition.

scenario: ChatGPT 需要保存和展示会话历史，但它不是转账、下单这类必须强一致的系统。
scenario_en: ChatGPT needs to save and show conversation history, but it is not a money-transfer or order-placement system that requires strict consistency.
optionExplanations: 强一致会让聊天变成要等所有副本确认才能回复，用户体验先崩溃，代价换不来实际收益。
完全不持久化等于每次刷新都丢历史，用户连昨天聊了什么都找不到，明显不可接受。
聊天记录不是转账，短暂看到旧消息好过让整个系统等一次完美同步，所以选可用性优先。
跨地域同步提交会把每次请求都拖到最慢那个区域的往返延迟，正常聊天场景负担不起。
optionExplanations_en: Strong consistency would make every reply wait on all replicas to ack — a real UX cost for no real benefit here.
Never persisting state means every refresh loses history; users couldn't even find yesterday's chat.
Chat history isn't a bank transfer — a brief stale read beats blocking the whole system for perfect sync, so availability wins.
Synchronous cross-region commits would tax every request with the slowest region's round trip, more than a normal chat needs to pay.

q: 补全 ChatGPT 的基础实体：
q_en: Fill in the base entities for ChatGPT:
text: 基础实体包括 {{User}}（带 free/paid tier）、{{Chat}}（单个对话线程）、{{Message}}（user 或 assistant 的一轮消息）；深挖后还会引入 {{Generation}} 表示一次推理运行。
why: User tier 后面影响公平调度，Chat 和 Message 支撑历史续聊。Generation 一开始不是必须实体，但当 runId、状态、取消、计费都出现后就值得建模。
why_en: The base entities are User, Chat, and Message, with Generation added later once an inference run needs its own lifecycle.

scenario: ChatGPT 后端给 web 和移动端提供 REST 接口，客户端不可信，身份只能由服务端 session 派生。
scenario_en: The ChatGPT backend exposes REST endpoints to untrusted web and mobile clients, so identity must come from the server-side session.
q: ChatGPT 的基础 API 需要覆盖哪些路径？（多选）
q_en: Which base API paths does ChatGPT need? (Choose all that apply.)
options: POST /chats 创建聊天
POST /chats/{chatId}/messages 发送 prompt 并流式返回
GET /chats 和 GET /chats/{chatId}/messages 分页读取历史
客户端在 body 里传 userId 让服务端信任
why: 创建、发送、历史列表和消息读取分别映射到 Chat 与 Message；userId 必须从 session/JWT 推导并做 ownership check。把 userId 放进请求体是可伪造的红旗。
why_en: The API covers creating chats, sending streamed messages, and paginated reads, while user identity must come from trusted auth context rather than the body.
options_en: POST /chats creates a new chat.
POST /chats/{chatId}/messages sends a prompt and streams the reply back.
GET /chats and GET /chats/{chatId}/messages paginate through history.
The client passes userId in the body and the server trusts it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端签发的身份令牌，用来在请求间证明用户身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token issued by the server that proves user identity across requests.

optionExplanations: POST /chats 是新建会话的入口，映射到 Chat 实体的创建动作。
POST /chats/{chatId}/messages 既发送 prompt 又承接流式回复，是这题最核心的写路径。
GET /chats 与消息列表分页读取，支撑历史续聊这个核心需求。
客户端自己在请求体里塞一个 userId，改一下 body 就能冒充别人，正确身份应该从已登录态（session 或 JWT）解析出来。
optionExplanations_en: POST /chats is the entry point that creates a new Chat entity.
POST /chats/{chatId}/messages both sends the prompt and carries the streamed reply back — the core write path.
GET /chats and the message list paginate through history, backing the resume-with-context requirement.
Trusting a client-supplied userId in the body means anyone can forge it by editing the request; identity must come from session/JWT instead.

rows: 校验 chat 属于 caller
只返回 caller 自己的

scenario: 聊天状态的读写是普通行存储，推理层则依赖昂贵 GPU，并且两者的扩缩容节奏完全不同。
scenario_en: Chat state reads and writes are ordinary row storage, while inference depends on expensive GPUs, and the two tiers scale at very different rates.
q: 为什么要拆出 Chat Service 和 Inference Service？
q_en: Why split Chat Service from Inference Service?
options: 让每条消息都写两个数据库
让客户端直接接管 GPU worker 的调度
为了完全不保存任何聊天历史记录
让编排层和 GPU 推理层能各自独立扩缩容与调度
why: Chat Service 负责认证后的编排和消息持久化，Inference Service 拥有 GPU worker。拆分后可以独立扩容、排队、调度 GPU，而不让普通请求层被 GPU 约束绑死。
why_en: Separating chat orchestration from GPU inference lets the cheap stateless tier and expensive worker tier scale and schedule independently.
whenOtherWins: 很小的内部 demo 可以把调用写在一个服务里；一旦 GPU 成为瓶颈，边界就必须清晰。
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> Chat[Chat Service]
Chat --> DB[(Chat DB)]
Chat --> Queue[Inference Queue]
Queue --> Worker[GPU Worker]
Worker --> Model[LLM Runtime]
tradeoff: 编排层与推理层独立扩缩容 vs 单服务实现简单
options_en: Route every message through two databases.
Let the client manage GPU workers directly.
Avoid persisting any chat history at all.
Let the cheap orchestration tier and the expensive GPU tier scale independently.
optionExplanations: 拆分服务不是为了重复写两次数据库，那只会增加一致性负担而不解决扩缩容问题。
把 GPU 调度暴露给客户端既不安全也不现实，调度权必须留在服务端。
拆分和是否保存历史无关，Chat Service 依然要持久化消息，只是不再兼职 GPU 编排。
编排层廉价无状态、GPU 层昂贵有状态，拆开后两条扩缩容曲线互不拖累，各自独立调度。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting services isn't about writing to two databases per message — that only adds consistency overhead without solving scaling.
Handing GPU scheduling to the client is neither safe nor practical; scheduling authority has to stay server-side.
The split has nothing to do with dropping history — Chat Service still persists messages, it just stops also owning GPU orchestration.
Orchestration is cheap and stateless while GPU inference is expensive and stateful, so splitting lets each scale on its own curve.

q: 把同步 MVP 的发送流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the synchronous MVP send flow in the right order:
steps: Chat Service 同步调用 Inference Service 并等待完整 completion
API Gateway 鉴权后转发给 Chat Service
客户端 POST /chats/{chatId}/messages
Chat Service 写入用户消息
Chat Service 写入 assistant message 并返回
why: 这个流程满足功能需求，但用户会等到完整回复生成完才看到结果。它故意暴露出 TTFT 和 admission control 两个后续深挖点。
why_en: The synchronous MVP works functionally but exposes blank-screen latency and missing admission control as the core problems.

scenario: 要存储 chats 和 messages，查询主要按 userId、chatId、createdAt 读取，数据模型简单且关系明确。
scenario_en: The system stores chats and messages, mostly read by userId, chatId, and createdAt; the data model is simple and relational.
q: 系统记录最合适的默认存储是什么？
q_en: What is the best default store for system records?
options: Postgres
Elasticsearch
Redis Pub/Sub
本地文件系统
why: 聊天与消息是简单、可索引、需要持久化的行数据，Postgres 是稳妥默认选择。文章也强调这里不是数据库选型难点，几乎任何合理持久化数据库都能工作。
why_en: Postgres is a sensible system of record because chats and messages are simple durable rows keyed by user and chat.
whenOtherWins: 如果核心需求变成跨历史全文搜索，Elasticsearch 会作为搜索索引补上；Redis Pub/Sub 不是 durable source of truth。
tradeoff: 简单持久化行存储 vs 全文搜索能力
options_en: Postgres.
Elasticsearch.
Redis Pub/Sub.
The local filesystem.
optionExplanations: 聊天与消息是简单、按 userId/chatId 索引的行数据，Postgres 这类关系型存储正好稳妥覆盖。
Elasticsearch 强在全文检索，但本题连搜索都不在范围内，用它当系统记录反而多余。
Redis Pub/Sub 不持久化，没有订阅者时消息直接丢，不能当聊天记录的唯一真相来源。
本地文件系统没有并发写保护也没有跨实例可见性，多实例服务根本没法安全共享它。
optionExplanations_en: Chats and messages are simple rows keyed by userId/chatId — a relational store like Postgres covers that solidly.
Elasticsearch shines at full-text search, but search isn't even in scope here, so it's overkill as the system of record.
Redis Pub/Sub doesn't persist anything — messages vanish with no subscriber listening, so it can't be the single source of truth.
A local filesystem has no concurrent-write protection or cross-instance visibility, so multiple service instances can't share it safely.

scenario: ChatGPT 对话可长达上百轮，模型按输入 token 计费，上下文窗口还有硬上限。
scenario_en: A ChatGPT conversation can run hundreds of turns, the model bills per input token, and the context window has a hard ceiling.
q: 每轮都把完整历史拼进 prompt 的主要后果是什么？
q_en: What is the main consequence of putting full history into every prompt?
options: 模型处理请求永远不会超出上下文窗口限制
输入成本和延迟随对话增长，最终撞上上下文窗口上限
可以完全不保存任何历史消息记录
会自动大幅提升 GPU 利用率表现
why: 全量历史是最简单的“记住对话”，但每轮都重复付费读取旧内容。长对话会同时带来成本、延迟和上下文窗口上限问题。
why_en: Replaying full history makes memory simple but causes input cost and prefill latency to grow until the context window is exceeded.
options_en: The model will never exceed its context window.
Input cost and latency grow with the conversation and eventually hit the context window limit.
It is fine to persist no message history at all.
It automatically raises GPU utilization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型处理输入 prompt、生成第一枚输出 token 之前的计算阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prefill is the compute phase where the model processes the input prompt before producing the first output token.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型单次能处理的最大 token 数量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The context window is the maximum number of tokens a model can process in one call.

optionExplanations: 上下文窗口有硬上限，历史越堆越多迟早会撞到它，说“永远不会超”正好说反了。
每轮都重放全部历史，输入 token 和 prefill 延迟会随对话变长持续增长，直到撞上窗口上限，这是全量历史最大的代价。
不保存历史听起来省事，但用户会发现模型“失忆”，完全违背带上下文续聊的需求。
把更多旧文本塞进 prompt 只会占用更多显存和计算，不会让 GPU 利用率变高，反而更浪费。
optionExplanations_en: The context window has a hard ceiling; piling up history eventually hits it — saying it 'never' will is backwards.
Replaying the full thread every turn keeps growing input tokens and prefill latency until you hit the context limit — that's the real cost.
Skipping history sounds cheap, but users would notice the model 'forgetting' everything, defeating the point of resuming with context.
Stuffing more old text into the prompt just eats more memory and compute; it doesn't raise GPU utilization, it wastes it.

scenario: 浏览器只需要在生成期间持续接收 token，prompt 已经通过 POST 发出，中途只有取消请求需要单独处理。
scenario_en: The browser only needs to receive tokens during generation; the prompt was already sent by POST, and only cancellation needs a separate path.
q: 对浏览器侧 token 推送，最贴合的传输方案是？
q_en: Which transport best fits browser-side token delivery?
options: 短轮询 status endpoint
UDP 组播
Server-Sent Events
每个 token 一个独立 HTTP 请求
why: SSE 是一条普通 HTTP 响应上的单向 server-to-client 流，正好匹配 token 下发。它避免 WebSocket 的双向状态成本，同时比轮询更快更平滑。
why_en: SSE fits token streaming because the browser only needs a one-way server-to-client stream after the prompt is submitted.
whenOtherWins: 如果客户端需要在同一连接上频繁双向交互，WebSocket 会更合适；如果只是低频状态检查，轮询也能接受。
tradeoff: 单向 server-push 简单性 vs 双向连接开销
options_en: Short-poll a status endpoint.
UDP multicast.
Server-Sent Events.
One separate HTTP request per token.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器向浏览器单向推送事件的 HTTP 流机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-Sent Events let a server push a one-way stream of events to the browser over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不保证送达、无连接的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless transport protocol that does not guarantee delivery.

optionExplanations: 轮询天然带着轮询间隔的延迟，够不到低 TTFT 的目标，还会在高峰期把请求量顶上去。
UDP 组播不保证送达也不是浏览器标准 API，网页拿不到可靠的组播通道。
SSE 是单向的普通 HTTP 流，天然匹配“只发不收”的 token 推送，还不用背 WebSocket 的双向连接状态。
给每个 token 开一条独立 HTTP 请求，连接建立开销会随 token 速率线性爆炸，完全不现实。
optionExplanations_en: Polling carries the poll interval as built-in delay, missing the low-TTFT target, and floods the backend at peak.
UDP multicast gives no delivery guarantee and isn't a standard browser API, so the page has no reliable way to join it.
SSE is a one-way stream over plain HTTP, a natural fit for a send-only token push, without WebSocket's connection state.
Opening one HTTP request per token makes connection overhead explode linearly with token rate — not realistic.

scenario: ChatGPT 有约 120k 并发生成流，产品要求首 token 数百毫秒内到，且逐字平滑出现。
scenario_en: ChatGPT carries about 120k concurrent streams and needs the first token within a few hundred milliseconds, arriving smoothly.
q: 为什么几百毫秒轮询不适合 LLM token 流？
q_en: Why is polling every few hundred milliseconds a poor fit for LLM token streams?
options: 轮询请求完全无法穿过负载均衡器
轮询方式只能在移动端使用
它要求把每个 token 都写入 Postgres
TTFT 被轮询间隔卡住，且请求量暴增
why: 120k 并发流每 300ms 轮询约等于 400k RPS，且多数为空响应。第一 token 还要等下一次 poll，用户看到的是一坨一坨出现而不是平滑流。
why_en: Polling delays the first token by the poll interval, creates huge mostly-empty request volume, and makes the stream arrive in chunks.
options_en: Polling requests cannot pass through a load balancer at all.
Polling only works on mobile clients.
It requires writing every token to Postgres.
TTFT is capped by the poll interval and request volume explodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从请求发出到第一个 token 出现的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTFT is the time from a request being sent to the first token appearing on screen.

optionExplanations: 轮询请求走的还是普通 HTTP，能正常穿过负载均衡器，这个说法本身就不成立。
轮询不是移动端专属技术，Web、桌面客户端一样可以轮询，这不是它的问题所在。
轮询本身不要求把每个 token 落库，它的问题在别处，跟 Postgres 写入无关。
把 300ms 轮询乘上 120k 条并发流，算下来接近 400k RPS 且大多空转，第一个 token 还要等下一个 poll 周期，用户看到的是一坨一坨蹦出来的文字。
optionExplanations_en: Polling is still plain HTTP and passes through a load balancer fine — this claim is simply false.
Polling isn't mobile-only; web and desktop clients poll the same way, so that's not the actual problem.
Polling doesn't require writing every token to a database — its real problem lies elsewhere.
120k concurrent streams polling every 300ms is close to 400k RPS, mostly empty, and the first token still waits for the next poll cycle, so users see text arrive in bursts.

scenario: GPU worker 要把 token 一个个推给 Chat Service，两个都是内部服务，需要类型化契约和高效复用连接。
scenario_en: A GPU worker must push tokens one by one to Chat Service; both are internal services that need a typed contract and efficient connection reuse.
q: 内部 worker → Chat Service 流最合适的协议是什么？
q_en: Which protocol best fits the internal worker-to-Chat-Service stream?
options: gRPC server-streaming
浏览器 EventSource
每个 token 写一次数据库再轮询
电子邮件 webhook
why: gRPC over HTTP/2 提供二进制 framing、连接复用和 protobuf 契约，适合服务间 stream。SSE 更适合浏览器边界，不是内部 worker API 的首选。
why_en: gRPC server streaming is a good internal hop because it gives efficient HTTP/2 multiplexing and a typed service contract.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是浏览器展示 token，SSE 更轻；如果 worker 只返回完整结果，普通 request/response 就够。
tradeoff: 服务间高效双工契约 vs 浏览器单向推送简单性
options_en: gRPC server-streaming.
Browser EventSource.
Write each token to the database and poll it.
Email webhook.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP/2 的服务间 RPC 框架，支持二进制 framing 和流式调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is an HTTP/2-based RPC framework for service-to-service calls that supports streaming.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览器用来接收 SSE 推送的原生 API。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EventSource is the browser API that receives a Server-Sent Events stream.

optionExplanations: gRPC 基于 HTTP/2，天然支持二进制帧、多路复用长连接和 protobuf 类型契约，服务间高频小包最省效率。
EventSource 是给浏览器边界设计的 API，服务器之间互相调用没有理由套一层浏览器协议。
把流式推送硬拗成每个 token 写库再轮询，等于把一个实时问题绕成一个数据库压力问题。
邮件既不是低延迟通道也没有流式语义，靠它传 token 会让用户等到地老天荒。
optionExplanations_en: gRPC over HTTP/2 natively gives binary framing, connection multiplexing, and a typed protobuf contract — the most efficient shape for frequent internal calls.
EventSource is built for the browser edge; there's no reason to wrap a browser-facing protocol between two backend services.
Forcing a streaming push into per-token database writes plus polling turns a real-time problem into a database-load problem.
Email is neither low-latency nor has streaming semantics — routing tokens through it would make users wait forever.

q: 补全浏览器与内部服务两段流的选择：
q_en: Fill in the two streaming choices for the browser and internal services:
text: 浏览器接收 token 用 {{SSE}}，因为它是单向 HTTP 推送；Inference Worker 到 Chat Service 用 {{gRPC server-streaming}}，因为它是服务间类型化流。
why: 两段流解决的是不同边界：用户边界追求简单兼容，内部边界追求高效契约。不要把一种协议硬套到所有连接上。
why_en: The browser edge uses SSE while the internal worker hop uses gRPC server streaming because each boundary has different protocol needs.

q: 让一个 Chat Service 实例同时持有 client SSE 和 worker gRPC 流的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of one Chat Service instance holding both the client SSE stream and the worker gRPC stream?
options: Postgres 无法写入 assistant 消息
部署/崩溃/扩缩容会切断长连接，还绑死 worker
浏览器无法正确显示中文字符
GPU 会自动进入空闲状态
why: 这个方案把无状态服务变成长连接中继，pod 替换会杀掉用户正在看的流。下一步需要让 worker 和持连接的 Chat Service 通过 runId 解耦。
why_en: Pinning a stream to one Chat Service instance makes deployments and crashes break long-lived generations and couples that instance to a worker.
scenario: Chat Service 是无状态、水平扩展的服务，会被频繁重新部署或自动扩缩容。
scenario_en: Chat Service is stateless and horizontally scaled, so instances may be redeployed or autoscaled frequently.
options_en: Postgres cannot write the assistant message.
Deploys, crashes, or autoscaling cut long connections and pin the instance to one worker.
The browser cannot render Chinese characters.
The GPU automatically goes idle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器向浏览器单向推送的 HTTP 流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is a one-way HTTP push stream from server to browser.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP/2 的服务间流式 RPC 框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is an HTTP/2-based streaming RPC framework used between services.

optionExplanations: 这个风险和 Postgres 写入能力无关，assistant 消息照样能正常落库。
把无状态服务变成长连接中继后，一次部署、崩溃或扩缩容就会直接砍断用户正在看的流，还把这个 worker 绑死在这台实例上。
中文渲染是编码问题，跟一个实例是否同时持有两条流没有任何关系。
GPU 不会因为服务拓扑变化自动空闲，它的忙闲只取决于有没有 token 要生成。
optionExplanations_en: This risk has nothing to do with Postgres — the assistant message still writes fine.
Turning a stateless service into a long-lived relay means one deploy, crash, or autoscale event cuts the stream a user is watching and pins that worker to this one instance.
Rendering Chinese text is an encoding concern, unrelated to whether one instance holds both streams.
The GPU doesn't go idle just because service topology changes — its business is only whether there are tokens left to generate.

scenario: worker 生成 token 的节点和持有浏览器 SSE 的 Chat Service 实例可能不是同一个，客户端重连后也可能落到新实例。
scenario_en: The worker generating tokens and the Chat Service instance holding the browser SSE stream may be different nodes, and reconnects may land on a new instance.
q: 第一步解耦 worker 和 Chat Service 可以用什么？
q_en: What can first decouple the worker from Chat Service?
options: 把每次生成的每个 token 都当新消息写入 Postgres
强制所有请求都 sticky 路由到同一个 pod 实例
按 runId 建 Redis Pub/Sub 频道解耦生成和连接
让浏览器直接建立连接连上 GPU worker
why: runId channel 让生成方和连接方只在逻辑 stream 上汇合，不关心彼此具体实例。这样重连后任意 Chat Service 都能订阅同一个 runId。
why_en: A runId-keyed pub/sub channel decouples token producers from whichever Chat Service instance holds the client connection.
whenOtherWins: 如果连接和 worker 生命周期很短且不会重连，直接中继更简单；如果需要 durable replay，纯 Pub/Sub 又不够。
tradeoff: 生成方与连接方解耦 vs 直接绑定的简单性
options_en: Write every token from each generation as a new Postgres message.
Force every request to stick-route to the same pod instance.
Create a runId-keyed Redis Pub/Sub channel to decouple generation from the connection.
Let the browser open a direct connection to the GPU worker.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式，发布者广播消息给当前在线的订阅者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is a publish-subscribe pattern where publishers broadcast to whichever subscribers are currently connected.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一次生成过程的唯一 ID，用来让生成方和连接方在逻辑上汇合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: runId is the unique identifier for one generation that lets producers and connections rendezvous logically.

optionExplanations: 把每次生成的每个 token 都当新消息写数据库，等于用持久化系统硬撑一个毫秒级的实时问题，延迟和写压力都会爆炸。
强制所有请求都 sticky 路由到同一个 pod 实例，又把 worker 焊死在这个实例上，重新部署照样断流，只是绕开了症状。
按 runId 建一个逻辑频道，生成方和连接方只靠这个 ID 汇合，谁在哪个实例上都无所谓，就算断线重连，随便换一个 Chat Service 实例也能接得上。
让浏览器直接建立连接连上 GPU worker，会把内部服务暴露到公网，还丢掉了 Chat Service 做鉴权和编排的这一层。
optionExplanations_en: Writing every token from each generation as a fresh database row forces a millisecond-scale real-time problem through a durable system — both latency and write pressure explode.
Forcing all requests to stick-route to the same pod instance just welds the worker to it; a redeploy still breaks the stream, it only hides the symptom.
A runId-keyed logical channel lets producer and connection rendezvous purely by that ID — it doesn't matter which instance either one is on, and any Chat Service can reattach after a reconnect.
Letting the browser open a direct connection to a GPU worker exposes an internal service to the public internet and drops the auth/orchestration layer Chat Service provides.

scenario: ChatGPT 用 Redis 做 token fanout，用户可能在生成中途断线重连，回答不能缺一段。
scenario_en: ChatGPT fans out tokens through Redis, and a user may drop and reconnect mid-generation without losing part of the answer.
q: Redis Pub/Sub 用在 token 流上的致命缺口是什么？
q_en: What is the fatal gap in using Redis Pub/Sub for token streaming?
options: 它会自动把每条 delta 拼接成完整的全量文本
它只能用来存储永久保留的消息记录
它不能按 runId 来命名 Pub/Sub channel
没有订阅者时消息不缓存，重连间隙发布的 token 会丢
why: Pub/Sub 是 fire-and-forget，只投递给当时在线的订阅者。部署或网络闪断期间丢的 delta 会让用户看到答案中间缺一段。
why_en: Redis Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget, so tokens published during a reconnect gap are lost to the live stream.
options_en: It automatically stitches every delta into the complete full text.
It can only store messages meant to be kept permanently.
It cannot name a Pub/Sub channel using the runId.
Messages are not buffered, so tokens published during a reconnect gap are lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式，只投递给当时在线的订阅者，不做持久化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub delivers messages only to subscribers connected at publish time and does not persist them.

optionExplanations: Pub/Sub 只是原样转发发布的内容，不会替你把每条 delta 拼接成完整的全量文本，这个说法反了。
Pub/Sub 恰恰相反——它只用来存储瞬时消息，谈不上“只能存永久保留的消息记录”。
channel 名字本来就是任意字符串，用 runId 来命名 Pub/Sub channel 完全没问题，这不是它的短板。
广播消息只发给当下在线的订阅者，没人在线就直接丢失，部署或网络抖动造成的重连间隙里发布的 token 就这样没了，用户看到的回复会中间缺一段。
optionExplanations_en: Pub/Sub just forwards whatever is published as-is — it won't stitch deltas into the complete full text for you, so this is backwards.
Pub/Sub is the opposite — it only holds messages briefly, so 'only stores messages meant to be kept permanently' doesn't apply.
A channel name is just an arbitrary string; naming a Pub/Sub channel by runId works fine — that's not where the weakness is.
Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget — with no subscriber listening, a message just disappears, so tokens published during a deploy or network blip vanish, leaving a visible gap in the user's answer.

scenario: 需要保持 runId 解耦，但客户端断线重连后必须补上 missed token，而不是等最终消息完成后再整体 refetch。
scenario_en: The design still needs runId decoupling, but after a client reconnects it must replay missed tokens instead of waiting to refetch the final message.
q: 应该把 token delta 写到哪里？
q_en: Where should token deltas be written?
options: Redis Stream，按 last-seen ID 用 XREAD 续读
Redis Pub/Sub 频道，完全不保留任何一点历史消息记录
把每一个 token 都单独写成一行 Postgres 记录当主路径
存进用户浏览器本地的 localStorage 长期存储空间里
why: Redis Stream 是短期 append-only log，XADD 每个 delta，XREAD 可从 last-seen ID 继续。它只为直播恢复服务，最终消息仍由 Postgres 持久化。
why_en: Redis Streams preserve short-lived token deltas so reconnecting clients can resume from the last seen entry without gaps.
whenOtherWins: 如果允许流中间丢 token、只关心最终结果，Pub/Sub 更简单；如果每个 token 都是合规记录，才考虑 durable database path。
tradeoff: 可重放的短期日志 vs fire-and-forget 广播
options_en: Redis Streams; Chat Service resumes with XREAD from the last-seen entry ID.
The Redis Pub/Sub channel, keeping absolutely no trace of message history.
Write every single token as its own persisted Postgres row on the main path.
The user's browser-local localStorage long-term storage space.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的 append-only 日志结构，可按 ID 顺序重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis Stream is an append-only log that can be replayed in order by entry ID.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从 Redis Stream 按位置读取新条目的命令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XREAD is the Redis command that reads new stream entries from a given position.

optionExplanations: 它是一份短期 append-only 的日志，XADD 写入、XREAD 能从 last-seen ID 续读，正好满足重连补洞而不用等最终消息。
上一张卡已经证明 Pub/Sub 会丢重连间隙的 token，不满足这里“必须补上 missed token”的要求。
把每个 token 都写一行 Postgres 记录当作主路径，会让数据库扛下本该是内存态的高频流量，代价太大。
存进浏览器本地 localStorage，换台设备就读不到，撑不起服务端的重连恢复。
optionExplanations_en: Redis Streams are a short-lived append-only log — XADD writes entries and XREAD resumes from the last-seen ID, exactly what's needed to replay gaps without waiting for the final message.
Pub/Sub was already shown to drop tokens published during a reconnect gap, so it fails the 'must replay missed tokens' requirement here.
Writing each token as one persisted Postgres row on the main path forces a database to absorb traffic that should live in memory — too costly.
The user's browser-local localStorage only lives on this device; nobody else, and not even a different device, can read it, so it can't back server-side reconnect recovery.

scenario: worker 已经生成一个 token delta，需要把它追加到 runId 的短期流里，供任意 Chat Service 重放。
scenario_en: A worker has produced one token delta and needs to append it to the short-lived runId stream so any Chat Service can replay it.
q: 哪条 Redis 命令最贴合这个写入？
q_en: Which Redis command best fits this write?
options: PUBLISH gen:{runId} "hello"
XADD gen:{runId} * token "hello"
SET gen:{runId} "hello"
LPUSH gen:{runId} "hello"
codeSample:
XADD gen:{runId} * token "hello"
XREAD BLOCK 5000 STREAMS gen:{runId} {lastSeenId}
why: XADD 追加带 ID 的条目，XREAD 可以从 lastSeenId 继续读取，正好支持重连补洞。PUBLISH 更轻但不会保存错过的 token。
why_en: XADD plus XREAD gives each token a stream entry ID, which lets a reconnecting client replay exactly the missed deltas.
whenOtherWins: 只做实时广播且允许断线丢消息时，PUBLISH 更省；只保存最终回复时，SET/数据库写入是另一个层次。
tradeoff: 可重放的 append-only 日志 vs 更轻量但不持久的广播
options_en: PUBLISH gen:{runId} "hello".
XADD gen:{runId} * token "hello".
SET gen:{runId} "hello".
LPUSH gen:{runId} "hello".

termDefinitions.meaning: 向 Redis Stream 追加一条带 ID 的新条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XADD appends a new ID-stamped entry to a Redis Stream.

optionExplanations: PUBLISH 是广播式的 fire-and-forget，没人在线就丢，不会把这条 delta 留下来给后来者补读。
XADD 把这个 delta 追加成一条带自增 ID 的日志条目，配合 XREAD 就能从上次的位置继续读，正是重连补洞要的语义。
SET 只会把这个 key 整个覆盖成最新值，之前的 delta 历史直接被冲掉，没法重放。
LPUSH 能保留多条元素，但它是普通 list，没有消费组、没有按位置续读的语义，硬凑重放会很别扭。
optionExplanations_en: PUBLISH is a fire-and-forget broadcast — with nobody listening it's gone, leaving nothing for a late reconnect to replay.
XADD appends this delta as a log entry with an auto-incrementing ID, and XREAD can resume from the last position — exactly the semantics reconnect-and-replay needs.
SET just overwrites the whole key with the newest value, wiping out the prior delta history — nothing left to replay.
LPUSH keeps multiple elements, but it's a plain list with no consumer groups or position-based resume — replaying from it would be awkward.

q: 补全 token 负载选择的原因：
q_en: Fill in why the token payload should be a delta:
text: token stream 应发布 {{delta}} 而不是 message-so-far，因为重复发送不断增长的完整前缀会让带宽接近 {{quadratic}} 开销。
why: 4,000 token 回复如果每次都发完整文本，会反复发送旧前缀。delta 让每个 token 只跨网络一次。
why_en: Streaming deltas avoids repeatedly sending the growing prefix, which would make bandwidth scale roughly quadratically with answer length.

q: 把最终 token streaming 流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the final token streaming flow in the right order:
steps: 客户端打开 runId 的 SSE 连接，落到任意 Chat Service
worker 生成 token 并 XADD 到 runId 的 Redis Stream
Chat Service 持久化用户消息并生成 runId
Chat Service XREAD 新条目并转发给浏览器
连接断开后新实例从 last-seen ID 继续读
why: 关键是 runId 把生成、读取和重连串起来，而 Redis Stream 提供短期 replay。这个流程同时满足低 TTFT 和不中断的 live stream。
why_en: The final streaming path uses runId plus Redis Streams so any Chat Service instance can forward live tokens and replay gaps after reconnects.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] -->|prompt| Chat[Chat Service]
Chat --> Queue[Bounded Queue]
Queue --> GPU[GPU Worker]
GPU -->|XADD deltas| Stream[(Redis Stream)]
Chat -->|XREAD| Stream
Chat -->|SSE| Client

q: 补全 Generation 实体的生命周期字段：
q_en: Fill in the lifecycle fields for the Generation entity:
text: Generation 代表一次推理尝试，包含 {{runId}}、chatId/messageId、status（queued/streaming/{{done}}/{{cancelled}}/failed）、model、input/output token count。
why: 一旦需要排队、流式恢复、取消、计费和状态查询，run 就不再只是返回值，而是系统里的实体。它把后续深挖都挂在同一个抽象上。
why_en: Generation becomes a first-class entity once an inference attempt needs status, streaming identity, cancellation, and token accounting.

scenario: 一次生成可能占用昂贵 GPU 30 秒，前端流量有突刺，worker 处理能力固定且远低于峰值提交速率。
scenario_en: One generation can occupy an expensive GPU for 30 seconds, frontend traffic spikes, and worker capacity is fixed far below peak submissions.
q: Chat Service 和 GPU worker 之间应该加入什么？
q_en: What should sit between Chat Service and GPU workers?
options: 每个 prompt 新建一台 GPU 机器
客户端直接随机挑 GPU
请求队列，由 worker 有容量时 pull
把 prompt 存进浏览器等待
why: 队列把突刺前端和稳定后端隔开，worker pull 可以天然表达容量。它还给 admission control、tier priority 和 backpressure 留出位置。
why_en: A queue between chat and workers absorbs bursts and lets GPU workers pull only when they have capacity.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务极短且资源充裕，同步调用更简单；如果需要严格实时控制硬件，专用调度器可能取代普通队列。
tradeoff: 请求队列削峰 vs 直接同步调用的简单性
options_en: Spin up a new GPU machine per prompt.
The client randomly picks a GPU directly.
A request queue that workers pull from when they have capacity.
Hold the prompt in the browser and wait.
optionExplanations: 每个 prompt 现开一台 GPU 机器，冷启动都比 30 秒生成还慢，根本来不及应对突刺流量。
让客户端自己随机挑 GPU，既没有全局视角也没法感知哪台已经满载，很容易把流量都砸在同一台上。
队列把突刺的前端和处理能力固定的后端隔开，worker 有容量时才 pull，天然给准入控制和优先级排序留出了位置。
把 prompt 攥在浏览器里等，等于把服务端该做的排队和调度丢给用户的标签页，网络一断就全丢了。
optionExplanations_en: Spinning up a fresh GPU machine per prompt has cold-start time slower than the 30-second generation itself — it can't react to bursty traffic at all.
Letting the client randomly pick a GPU has no global view and can't sense which one is already saturated, so traffic easily piles onto the same machine.
A queue separates bursty front-end traffic from fixed back-end capacity — workers pull only when they have room, naturally leaving space for admission control and priority.
Holding the prompt in the browser pushes server-side queuing and scheduling onto the user's tab, and it's all lost the moment the connection drops.

scenario: ChatGPT 峰值 20k prompts/sec 但 GPU 容量固定，过载会持续几分钟而不是几秒突刺。
scenario_en: ChatGPT peaks at 20k prompts per second against fixed GPU capacity, and overload lasts minutes rather than a brief spike.
q: 只有一个无界队列但没有 backpressure 会导致什么？
q_en: What happens with one unbounded queue and no backpressure?
options: 所有用户请求都会马上收到 429 拒绝
系统会自动减少用户输入的 token 数量
GPU 利用率必然达到 100% 且天然公平
持续过载时排队时间无限增长，用户不知道要等几秒还是几分钟
why: 队列只能吸收短暂突刺，不能创造 GPU 容量。队列深度不封顶时，延迟会无上限增长，产品体验变成永远转圈。
why_en: An unbounded queue turns sustained overload into unbounded wait time instead of a clear admission decision.
options_en: All user requests immediately receive a 429 rejection.
The system automatically reduces the user's input token count.
GPU utilization automatically reaches 100 percent and stays fair.
Under sustained overload, wait time grows unbounded and users cannot tell if it's seconds or minutes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在过载时主动限制或拒绝新请求，避免延迟无限增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure is a system deliberately limiting or rejecting new work under overload instead of letting latency grow unbounded.

optionExplanations: 无界队列的问题恰恰是它从不拒绝请求，所以不会有“所有用户马上收到 429”这种事发生。
队列深度和 token 预算是两码事，队列本身不会去动用户输入的长度。
队列排得再满也造不出新的 GPU 容量，利用率不会因此自动变成 100% 或者公平。
队列只能吸收短暂突刺，一旦持续过载，深度不封顶意味着等待时间跟着无限往上涨，用户完全不知道是要等几秒还是几分钟。
optionExplanations_en: An unbounded queue's whole problem is that it never rejects anything, so 'every user immediately gets a 429' can't happen.
Queue depth and token budgets are separate concerns — the queue itself never touches how long a user's input is.
A fuller queue doesn't create new GPU capacity; utilization doesn't automatically become 100 percent or fair just because of it.
A queue only absorbs short bursts — once overload is sustained, an uncapped depth means wait time climbs without bound, and users can't tell if it's seconds or minutes.

scenario: GPU 每次前向都要把巨大模型权重流过计算单元，单序列 decode 会让昂贵硬件大部分时间等内存带宽。
scenario_en: Each GPU forward pass must move huge model weights through compute units, so single-sequence decoding leaves expensive hardware waiting on memory bandwidth.
q: 提升 LLM worker 利用率的核心 serving 技术是什么？
q_en: What core serving technique improves LLM worker utilization?
options: 连续批处理（continuous batching）
让每一个用户都独占一整个专属的 GPU worker
把完整的回复内容先整体写进 Postgres 再统一发送
给每个请求都加一个固定的 sleep 延迟让节奏变平滑
why: continuous batching 让一个 forward pass 同时推进多条序列一 token，并在序列结束时立刻补入新请求。这样一次读取权重可以服务几十条生成。
why_en: Continuous batching keeps the GPU busy by advancing many sequences per forward pass and replacing finished ones immediately.
whenOtherWins: 如果模型很小、请求稀疏，简单单请求执行足够；高并发大模型 serving 才需要这套复杂调度。
tradeoff: 跨序列共享一次权重读取 vs 单序列独占 GPU
options_en: Continuous batching.
Give every single user their own entire dedicated GPU worker.
Write the full reply content all at once to Postgres before sending it.
Add a fixed sleep delay to every request to smooth out pacing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多条生成序列共享同一次前向计算，完成的序列立即被新请求替换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous batching advances many generation sequences together in one forward pass and replaces finished ones immediately.

optionExplanations: 这项技术能在一次前向计算里同时推进几十条序列各一个 token，序列结束立刻补新请求进来，权重只搬一次却能服务很多条生成。
让每一个用户都独占一整个专属的 GPU worker，等于放弃了共享一次权重读取的机会，GPU 大部分时间反而在等内存带宽。
把完整的回复内容先整体写进 Postgres 再统一发送，只是换了个持久化顺序，跟计算单元有没有被喂饱毫无关系。
给每个请求都加一个固定的 sleep 延迟让节奏变平滑，只是人为拖慢，既不会让 GPU 忙起来，也不会真正让流量变平滑。
optionExplanations_en: Continuous batching advances dozens of sequences one token each per forward pass, immediately backfilling finished slots — one weight read now serves many generations.
Dedicating a whole GPU worker to every single user gives up the chance to share a single weight read, so the GPU spends more time waiting on memory bandwidth.
Writing the full reply content to Postgres all at once before sending it just reorders persistence — it has nothing to do with keeping compute units fed.
Adding a fixed sleep delay to every request only artificially slows the pace; it neither keeps the GPU busy nor genuinely smooths traffic.

q: 补全 GPU batching 的直觉：
q_en: Fill in the intuition behind GPU batching:
text: LLM decode 常被说成 {{memory-bandwidth}} bound；batching 的收益是一次搬运模型权重，顺手为 {{many sequences}} 各生成一个 token。
why: 权重常驻高带宽显存，但每步仍要流过计算单元。批量越满，同一次权重读取摊到的 token 越多，利用率越高。
why_en: Decode is often memory-bandwidth bound, so batching makes one weight read produce tokens for many sequences.

q: 把带 backpressure 和 continuous batching 的生成调度排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the generation scheduling flow with backpressure and continuous batching in the right order:
steps: worker 把请求加入正在运行的 batch
Chat Service 提交带 runId 和 token-cost estimate 的 generation
batch 每步生成 token 并写入 runId stream
admission control 根据队列深度决定接收、延后或拒绝
完成或取消后从 batch 移除并拉取下一项
why: admission control 先决定是否值得排队，worker 只在容量允许时拉取。continuous batching 则在 worker 内部提高每次 forward pass 的产出。
why_en: Admission control bounds waiting while continuous batching increases the amount of useful GPU work per decoding step.
diagram:
flowchart TD
Req[Generation Request] --> Budget[Check token budget]
Budget --> Queue[Tier queue]
Queue --> Batch[Continuous batch]
Batch --> GPU[GPU decode]
GPU --> Stream[Token stream]

scenario: ChatGPT 用户的 prompt 长度能差几十倍，GPU 成本按输入输出 token 计，现在要选限流指标。
scenario_en: ChatGPT prompt lengths vary by tens of times and GPU cost tracks input and output tokens, so you must pick a throttling metric.
q: 为什么普通 requests-per-minute 不是 ChatGPT 公平性的好指标？
q_en: Why is plain requests-per-minute a poor fairness metric for ChatGPT?
options: 限流器在技术上完全无法用 Redis 来实现
请求数不等于 GPU 成本，长 prompt 更贵
这种按请求限流只能应用于匿名访问用户
它会强制把每一个 token 都持久化保存
why: LLM 成本主要由输入输出 token 和模型大小决定，不是 HTTP 请求数。按请求限流会让巨大 prompt 低估成本，也会误伤许多短请求。
why_en: Request counts are the wrong fairness unit because GPU cost is driven by token and model compute, not by the number of HTTP calls.
tradeoff: 按 token/compute 计量 vs 按请求数计量
options_en: A rate limiter technically cannot be implemented on Redis at all.
Request count is not GPU cost; a long prompt can cost more than many short ones.
This request-based limiting only applies to anonymous visiting users.
It forces every single token to be persisted to storage.
optionExplanations: 限流器在技术上完全可以用 Redis 来实现（比如令牌桶计数），技术上不是问题，问题不在这里。
一次请求可能带一个字的 prompt，也可能带几千 token 的长文，真正吃 GPU 的是 token 和算力，不是请求这个计数单位。
这种按请求限流只能应用于匿名访问用户的说法站不住脚，登录用户一样适用，跟匿名与否没有关系。
限流策略选什么单位计费，和它会强制把每一个 token 都持久化保存完全是两件事。
optionExplanations_en: A rate limiter technically cannot be implemented on Redis at all — that claim is false; a token-bucket counter works fine.
One request might carry a one-word prompt or a several-thousand-token essay; what actually eats the GPU is tokens and compute, not the request count.
Rate-limiting by request applies just as well to logged-in users — it has nothing to do with being anonymous.
Which unit a rate limiter counts by has nothing to do with whether every token gets forced into persisted storage.

scenario: 一个用户可能发很长 prompt 或要求很长输出，真正稀缺资源是 GPU token compute；同时系统有 free 和 paid tier。
scenario_en: One user may send a very long prompt or request a long output, the scarce resource is GPU token compute, and the product has free and paid tiers.
q: 公平与商业优先级的组合策略是什么？
q_en: What strategy combines fairness with business priority?
options: 全站所有用户共用一个全局 RPM 限流上限
所有用户请求完全按随机顺序排队处理
按用户 token 预算 + tier 优先队列
只按访问 IP 限流，完全不区分具体账号
why: 公平的计量单位是 token 而不是请求：成本 ≈ input tokens + output tokens × 模型系数。per-user token 预算防单人吃光，tier 队列只在容量紧张时倾斜。
why_en: The unit of fairness is tokens, not requests, since cost is roughly input tokens plus output tokens times a model factor, so a per-user token budget stops one heavy user from eating capacity while the tier queue only tilts things when capacity is tight.
whenOtherWins: 普通 REST API 的成本近似每请求相同，简单 RPM 或并发上限就可能足够。
tradeoff: 按用户 token 预算 + 分级优先级 vs 全局统一限流
options_en: One shared global RPM cap across the entire site.
Queue every user's request in a fully random order.
Per-user token/compute budgets plus a tier-aware priority queue.
Rate-limit only by visiting IP, ignoring the account entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户账号的等级（如 free/paid），影响调度优先级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tier is the account level, such as free or paid, that affects scheduling priority.

optionExplanations: 全站所有用户共用一个全局 RPM 限流上限，分不清谁是付费谁是免费，也管不住单个大 prompt 的真实成本。
所有用户请求完全按随机顺序排队处理，等于放弃了产品想给付费用户的优先级，跟“公平 + 商业优先级”背道而驰。
按用户设 token/compute 预算防止一个重度用户吃光资源，再叠加 tier 优先队列让付费在紧张时体验更好，两件事分开解决刚好覆盖公平和商业优先级。
只按访问 IP 限流，完全不区分具体账号，一个 IP 后面可能有很多用户，也识别不出谁是付费用户。
optionExplanations_en: One shared global RPM cap across the entire site can't tell paid from free apart, and it can't cap the real cost of one giant prompt either.
Queuing every user's request in fully random order gives up any priority for paid users, working against the goal of combining fairness with business priority.

Per-user token/compute budgets stop one heavy user from hogging resources, and a tier-aware queue on top gives paid users a better experience when capacity is tight — two mechanisms covering fairness and priority.
Rate-limiting only by visiting IP, ignoring the account entirely, means many users can sit behind one IP and it can't tell who's paying.

scenario: ChatGPT 容量紧张时要先保住付费体验，但 free 用户是增长漏斗，不能被长期饿死。
scenario_en: When ChatGPT capacity is tight, paid experience comes first, but free users feed growth and cannot be starved indefinitely.
q: 容量紧张时，对不同 tier 的降级手段包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: When capacity is tight, which degradation moves can apply to different tiers? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 优先 throttle 或 defer free 用户
把部分 free 请求路由到更小更便宜的模型
付费和免费永远严格同等待遇
给 free 流量保留一个最低容量地板，避免长期饥饿
why: 文章强调付费优先但不能让 free 永久饿死。常见策略是限流、延后、降模型，同时保留最低份额。
why_en: Degradation can throttle, defer, or downgrade free traffic first while reserving a floor so it is not starved indefinitely.
options_en: Throttle or defer free-tier users first.
Route some free requests to a smaller, cheaper model.
Paid and free users always get strictly equal treatment.
Reserve a minimum capacity floor for free traffic so it is never starved.
optionExplanations: 先限流或延后 free 用户是最直接的削峰手段，把稀缺容量先留给愿意付费的人。
把部分 free 请求路由到更小模型，换取更低成本和更高吞吐，用户体验略降但仍可用。
付费和免费永远严格同等待遇违背了这里“付费优先”的商业目标，不是本题会采用的策略。
给 free 流量留一个不能再往下砍的容量地板，避免免费用户在持续高峰期被完全饿死。
optionExplanations_en: Throttling or deferring free users first is the most direct way to shed load, saving scarce capacity for paying users.
Routing some free requests to a smaller model trades a little quality for lower cost and higher throughput, staying usable.
Treating paid and free as always strictly equal contradicts the 'paid gets priority' business goal — not a move this design takes.
Reserving a floor that free traffic can't be cut below prevents free users from being starved indefinitely during sustained peaks.

scenario: ChatGPT 在 admission 时就要扣用户 token 预算，可输出长度直到生成结束才真正确定。
scenario_en: ChatGPT debits a user token budget at admission time, yet the real output length is only known once generation finishes.
q: 为什么 token budget 必须允许事后 reconcile？
q_en: Why must a token budget allow reconciliation after the request finishes?
options: SSE 协议无法携带 token 内容
Redis 数据库无法存储整数类型
付费用户完全不需要用量 quota
输出长度只能估计，真实值等完成才知道
why: 提交时只能根据 prompt 长度和 max output 估算成本，实际输出到结束才确定。软预算可以先 admission，完成后按真实用量校正。
why_en: Token budgets need reconciliation because output length is only estimated before generation and known after completion.
options_en: SSE cannot carry token content.
Redis cannot store integers.
Paid users need no usage quota at all.
Output length can only be estimated before completion, the real count is known afterward.
optionExplanations: 这里的 token 是用量计费单位，跟 SSE 能不能传输内容是两件不相关的事。
Redis 原生就能存整数并做计数器，这从来不是限制，说反了。
付费层同样有用量上限，只是额度更宽松，不是完全没有 quota。
生成开始前谁也不知道模型最终会吐多少字，只能拿输入长度和设定的输出上限估个大概，等跑完才有准数，所以预算得先放行、再事后校正。
optionExplanations_en: Here 'token' means a usage unit, unrelated to whether SSE can carry content.
Redis natively stores integers and does counting fine — this isn't a real limit, the claim has it backwards.
Paid tiers still have a usage cap, just a looser one — it's not zero quota.

At submission time cost can only be estimated from prompt length and max output; the real count is known once generation finishes, so the budget must admit optimistically and reconcile against actual usage afterward.

scenario: 长对话每轮都发送完整历史，既贵又可能超出 context window，但用户仍希望模型记得早期内容。
scenario_en: Long chats become expensive and may exceed the context window if every turn sends full history, but users still expect the model to remember earlier details.
q: 最合理的组合方案是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable combined context strategy?
options: 摘要 + 最近原文 + prefix caching
只保留最近 N 轮，旧内容全部丢弃
每轮都发送全量历史，直到报错失败
把所有旧消息塞进 response header
why: summary 压缩旧上下文，最近原文保留高价值细节，prefix caching 让稳定前缀便宜。三者一起控制窗口、成本和记忆质量。
why_en: A rolling summary plus recent verbatim turns plus prefix caching balances memory quality, context-window limits, and input cost.
whenOtherWins: 短对话可以直接全量历史；一次性匿名问答可以只用当前 prompt；强事实检索场景还可加 retrieval。
diagram:
flowchart LR
History[Recent messages] --> Builder[Prompt builder]
Summary[Rolling summary] --> Builder
Docs[Retrieved context] --> Builder
Builder --> Model[LLM]
Model --> Reply[Assistant reply]
tradeoff: 分层记忆（摘要+原文+前缀缓存） vs 简单截断
options_en: A rolling summary plus recent verbatim turns plus prefix caching.
Keep only the last N turns and drop everything older.
Send the full history every turn until it fails.
Stuff all old messages into a response header.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用稳定 prompt 前缀已算好的 KV cache，避免重复计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prefix caching reuses the already-computed KV cache for a stable prompt prefix instead of recomputing it.

optionExplanations: 摘要负责把旧内容压成可复用的 gist，最近几轮留住原话细节，再靠前缀缓存省掉对不变部分的重复计算，三者分工不同，合起来控住记忆质量、窗口和成本。
只留最近 N 轮能硬控成本，但第 N+1 轮之外的内容说丢就丢，用户会觉得模型突然失忆。
每轮都发全量历史直到报错，等于放任成本和延迟随对话线性增长，最后被上下文窗口硬顶死。
response header 是给元数据用的，塞进大段历史文本既不符合语义也会撞上 header 大小限制。
optionExplanations_en: A summary compresses old content, recent verbatim turns keep high-value detail, and prefix caching skips recomputing the stable prefix — together they manage memory quality, window size, and cost.
Keeping only the last N turns bounds cost, but everything past turn N+1 is gone for good, so the model feels like it suddenly forgot.
Sending the full history every turn until it errors just lets cost and latency grow linearly until the context window hard-stops it.
Response headers are for metadata; cramming long history text into one breaks that convention and runs into header size limits.

scenario: 为了快速给一个长对话做成本上限，先只取最近 N 条消息，但仍要保持模型看到的顺序正确。
scenario_en: To cap cost for a long chat quickly, the system first fetches only the latest N messages, but the model must still see them in the correct order.
q: 这段查询后还必须做什么？
q_en: What must happen after this query?
options: 直接把 DESC 顺序的结果原样喂给模型
把结果再翻回 createdAt 升序后拼 prompt
把所有 assistant 消息记录都删除掉
直接把查询的 LIMIT 改成无穷大
codeSample:
SELECT * FROM messages
WHERE chatId = $1
ORDER BY createdAt DESC
LIMIT $2;
why: DESC + LIMIT 是为了拿最新 N 条，拼 prompt 时必须恢复时间正序。否则模型会先看到未来回复再看到旧问题，语义会乱。
why_en: The newest rows are fetched descending for efficiency, but the prompt must be assembled in chronological order.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据库支持反向窗口后稳定排序，也可以在查询层直接返回正序；全量历史短小时不需要 LIMIT。
tradeoff: 恢复时间正序保证语义 vs 直接使用查询返回顺序
options_en: Feed the model the rows in DESC order as returned.
Flip the rows back to ascending createdAt order before building the prompt.
Delete every assistant message record entirely.
Change the query's LIMIT to unbounded.
optionExplanations: 直接把 DESC 顺序的结果原样喂给模型，模型会先看到最新回复再看到旧问题，时间线倒着讲故事，语义全乱。
DESC + LIMIT 只是为了高效取出最新 N 条，拼 prompt 前必须把它们翻回 createdAt 升序，模型才能按真实时间顺序理解对话。
这条查询跟要不要把所有 assistant 消息记录都删除掉完全无关，删除只会丢数据不会解决排序问题。
直接把查询的 LIMIT 改成无穷大，等于放弃了控成本的初衷，又变回了发送全量历史的老问题。
optionExplanations_en: Feeding the model rows in DESC order as returned means it sees the newest reply before the old question — the timeline runs backward and the meaning breaks.
DESC plus LIMIT is only there to fetch the latest N rows efficiently; before building the prompt they must be flipped back to ascending createdAt so the model reads the real chronological order.
This query has nothing to do with deleting every assistant message record — deleting rows just loses data, it doesn't fix ordering.
Changing the query's LIMIT to unbounded gives up the whole point of capping cost, sliding right back into the full-history problem.

scenario: ChatGPT 长对话要控上下文成本，但用户常在第 30 轮回头引用第 3 轮说过的事实。
scenario_en: Long ChatGPT chats must cap context cost, yet users often refer back at turn 30 to a fact stated at turn 3.
q: 最近 N 轮截断相比 rolling summary 的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with keeping only the most recent N turns compared with a rolling summary?
options: 截断成本不固定
截断会增加输出 token 数
旧事实会突然消失，用户会感觉模型失忆
summary 不能和 prefix caching 共存
why: 只保留最近 N 轮能硬控成本，但第 N+1 轮外的信息直接丢失。summary 用有损压缩保留旧上下文的 gist，体验更连续。
why_en: Recent-turn truncation bounds cost but creates abrupt amnesia, while summaries preserve older context in compressed form.
tradeoff: 硬截断成本可控 vs 摘要保留记忆连续性
options_en: Truncation cost is not fixed.
Truncation increases output token count.
Old facts vanish abruptly and the model feels like it forgot.
Summaries cannot coexist with prefix caching.
optionExplanations: 只保留最近 N 轮恰恰是为了把成本钉死在一个上限上，说它成本不固定是说反了。
截断只影响喂给模型的输入长度，跟模型要生成多少输出 token 没有直接关系。
第 N+1 轮之外的信息说没就没，用户提过的旧事实突然从上下文消失，体验上就是模型“失忆”了；summary 用有损压缩留住这些 gist，体验更连续。
summary 完全可以设计成稳定前缀的一部分，只要不频繁重写就能和 prefix caching 共存，两者不冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping only the last N turns is precisely how you pin cost to a hard ceiling — saying its cost isn't fixed has it backwards.
Truncation only shrinks what's fed into the model as input; it has no direct effect on how many tokens the model chooses to output.

Anything past turn N+1 just vanishes — facts the user mentioned earlier disappear from context without warning, which feels like the model 'forgot'; a summary keeps a lossy gist of them instead, so the experience stays continuous.
A summary can absolutely be part of a stable prefix — as long as it isn't rewritten often, it coexists with prefix caching just fine.

scenario: ChatGPT 每轮 prompt 的 system prompt 和旧消息几乎不变，只有尾部新增，目标是压 TTFT 和输入成本。
scenario_en: In ChatGPT each turn reuses a nearly identical system prompt and old messages, appending only a tail, and you want lower TTFT and input cost.
q: prefix caching 对 TTFT 和成本的帮助来自哪里？
q_en: Where do prefix caching savings for TTFT and cost come from?
options: 让 Redis Stream 变成永久持久化存储
把所有输出 token 都缓存进 CDN 节点
减少数据库里存储的行数总量
复用稳定前缀的 KV cache，避免重算旧上下文
why: 同一对话的 system prompt、summary 和旧消息大多稳定，KV cache 可复用这些前缀。只处理新增尾部会降低 prefill 延迟和输入成本。
why_en: Prefix caching reuses KV state for stable prompt prefixes, reducing prefill latency and repeated input compute.
options_en: Turn Redis Streams into permanent durable storage.
Cache every output token inside a CDN node.
Reduce the number of database rows stored.
Reuse the KV cache for a stable prefix instead of recomputing old context.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推理时缓存已计算的 attention key/value，避免重复计算历史 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The KV cache stores already-computed attention keys and values so past tokens are not recomputed.

optionExplanations: prefix caching 跟 Redis Stream 是否持久化完全是两回事，它作用在模型推理这一层。
CDN 缓存的是静态资源分发，不是模型推理过程中的 attention 状态，这个说法张冠李戴。
它省的是计算，不是数据库存储行数，两者的优化对象不是一回事。
这场对话里基本不变的内容——system prompt、摘要、旧消息——可以当成稳定前缀，直接复用它们早就算好的 KV cache 不用重算，prefill 延迟和输入成本自然就降了。
optionExplanations_en: Prefix caching has nothing to do with whether Redis Streams persist — it operates at the model-inference layer.
CDN caching is about static asset delivery, not the attention state produced during inference — this mixes up two different things.
What it saves is compute, not database row count — those are different optimization targets entirely.

The system prompt, summary, and older messages in the same conversation mostly stay stable, so reusing the already-computed KV cache for that prefix skips recomputation, cutting prefill latency and input cost.

scenario: ChatGPT 已开启 prefix caching，KV cache 只有在 prompt 前缀逐字节稳定时才命中。
scenario_en: ChatGPT already runs prefix caching, and the KV cache only hits when the prompt prefix stays byte-for-byte stable.
q: 为什么 rolling summary 不应每一轮都重写？
q_en: Why should the rolling summary not be rewritten on every turn?
options: 频繁改写 summary 会让 prompt 前缀失效
summary 一定会比原文更长更详细
Postgres 数据库无法存储 summary
SSE 协议不支持传输 summary 内容
why: prefix caching 依赖稳定前缀；summary 每轮重写会让缓存命中率下降。更好的做法是按较慢 cadence 折叠旧消息。
why_en: Rewriting the summary every turn changes the prefix and defeats prefix-cache reuse.
options_en: Rewriting the summary often changes the prompt prefix and invalidates the prefix cache.
A summary is always longer than the original text.
Postgres cannot store a summary.
SSE does not support summaries.
optionExplanations: 它依赖一段稳定不变的前缀作为缓存键，每轮都重写 summary 就等于每轮都在改这段前缀，已经缓存的 KV 状态直接作废。
摘要存在的意义正是比原文短，说它一定更长更详细刚好说反了。
Postgres 能存任意长度文本，不存在存不下 summary 这回事。
SSE 只负责把字节流推给浏览器，完全不关心内容是不是摘要，这跟它无关。
optionExplanations_en: Prefix caching depends on a stable prefix; rewriting the summary every turn changes that prefix every time, invalidating the already-cached KV state.
A summary exists specifically to be shorter than the original — claiming it's always longer has it backwards.
Postgres can store text of any length, so 'can't store a summary' isn't a real limitation.
SSE just pushes bytes to the browser; it doesn't care whether the content is a summary or not — unrelated to this.

scenario: 用户点击停止生成；token 下发走 SSE 单向流，不能把取消消息反向塞回同一条 EventSource。
scenario_en: The user clicks stop generation; token delivery uses a one-way SSE stream, so cancellation cannot be sent back through the same EventSource.
q: 取消一次 Generation 应该怎么做？
q_en: How should one Generation be cancelled?
options: 只是简单关闭浏览器标签页就自动触发取消了
POST 一个 cancel 端点，标记状态并通知 worker
非要等完整 30 秒生成全部结束后再丢弃掉
只把 Redis Stream 数据直接整个删除掉就够了
why: SSE 是单向的，取消走单独 HTTP side-channel。worker 在 token batch 间检查 cancel 信号，看到后把 sequence 从 batch 中移除并释放 GPU。
why_en: Cancellation should be an explicit side-channel request that marks the Generation cancelled and tells the worker to drop the sequence.
whenOtherWins: 双向 WebSocket 可以在同一连接发 stop；但对纯 token 下发，SSE 加 HTTP cancel 更简单。
diagram:
flowchart LR
Cancel[Cancel request] --> Gen[Generation row canceled]
Gen --> Queue[Remove pending job]
Gen --> Worker[Stop active decode]
Worker --> Final[Persist final state]
tradeoff: 显式 side-channel 取消信号 vs 依赖连接关闭
options_en: Just simply closing the browser tab automatically cancels it.
POST a cancel endpoint that marks the status and notifies the worker.
Insist on waiting for the full 30-second generation to finish, then discard it.
Just deleting the Redis Stream data entirely is enough on its own.
optionExplanations: 只是关闭浏览器标签页只是断开了这一条 SSE 连接，worker 那边完全不知道要停，生成还在后台继续跑。
取消信号没法通过单向的 SSE 逆向传回去，得另开一条独立的 side-channel：POST 一个 cancel 端点，标记 Generation 状态并通知 worker 停止解码。
等待完整 30 秒生成全部结束后再丢弃，等于什么也没省，GPU 时间已经全部花掉了。
只把 Redis Stream 直接删除掉挡不住 worker 继续往里 XADD，也没有真正告诉 worker 停止解码，治标不治本。
optionExplanations_en: Simply closing the browser tab only drops one SSE connection; the worker has no idea it should stop, so generation keeps running in the background.
SSE is one-way, so cancellation needs its own side-channel: POST a cancel endpoint that marks the Generation's status and tells the worker to stop.
Waiting for the full 30-second generation to finish before discarding it saves nothing — the GPU time is already spent.
Just deleting the Redis Stream entry doesn't stop the worker from still XADDing into it and never actually tells it to stop decoding — treats the symptom, not the cause.

scenario: ChatGPT 支持 SSE 断线重连和后台继续生成，移动端网络抖动每天都会发生。
scenario_en: ChatGPT supports SSE reconnect and keeps generating in the background, and mobile networks drop connections every day.
q: 为什么“关闭 tab / 断线”不能等同于取消生成？
q_en: Why should closing the tab or losing the connection not count as cancelling generation?
options: 因为 Postgres 只在标签页打开时才写入
因为浏览器网络连接永远不会断开
系统支持断线重连和后台继续生成，用户可能回来
因为 Redis Stream 无法设置 TTL 过期
why: Redis Stream 和 SSE reconnect 的目的就是让临时断线不毁掉回答。取消必须是明确用户意图，否则网络抖动会浪费已经排队和生成的工作。
why_en: A dropped connection is not cancellation because the system intentionally supports reconnecting to an ongoing or completed generation.
tradeoff: 网络中断 vs 用户主动取消意图
options_en: Because Postgres only writes while the tab is open.
Because the browser connection never drops.
The system supports reconnecting and keeps generating in the background, so the user may come back.
Because Redis Streams cannot have a TTL.
optionExplanations: Postgres 的写入完全不看浏览器标签页是否打开，服务端进程该写还是写。
网络连接当然会断——手机切网络、Wi-Fi 抖动都很常见，这个前提本身不成立。
系统专门设计了断线重连和后台继续生成，用户可能只是网络抖了一下还会回来看结果，把断线当取消会白白浪费已经排队和生成的工作。
Redis Stream 完全可以设置 TTL 自动到期，这不是限制它当取消信号的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Postgres writes don't depend on whether a browser tab is open — the server process writes regardless.
Connections absolutely do drop — phones switch networks, Wi-Fi blips — so this premise is simply false.

The system is deliberately built to support reconnecting and keep generating in the background; the user may just have a network blip and come back, so treating a drop as cancellation wastes work already queued and generated.
A Redis Stream can perfectly well be set to lapse on a TTL — that's not a reason it can't serve as a cancel signal.

scenario: ChatGPT 的 serving 主线（流式、GPU 调度、上下文成本）已讲完，面试还剩十分钟深挖。
scenario_en: The ChatGPT serving core, streaming, GPU scheduling and context cost, is done and ten minutes of deep dive remain.
q: 除了 serving 系统本身，还有哪些方向值得继续深挖？（多选）
q_en: Beyond the serving system itself, which topics are worth deeper follow-up? (Choose all that apply.)
options: prompt 与输出的 safety/moderation
模型并行与 GPU 间互联
speculative decoding
把聊天历史完全存在浏览器 cookie
why: 额外方向包括安全审核、模型如何跨多 GPU、speculative decoding、小模型路由/语义缓存、多模态和跨聊天记忆。cookie 不是合理的历史存储方案。
why_en: Additional deep dives include moderation, multi-GPU model serving, speculative decoding, cheaper routing and caching, multimodal input, and cross-chat memory.
options_en: Safety and moderation for prompts and outputs.
Model parallelism and inter-GPU interconnect.
Speculative decoding.
Storing chat history entirely in a browser cookie.
optionExplanations: prompt 和输出的安全审核不在这次 serving 深挖里，但正式产品少不了它，值得单独展开。
多 GPU 互联和模型并行解决的是单卡放不下大模型的问题，跟这道题的调度和公平是不同的深挖方向。
它靠小模型先猜、大模型一次验证多个候选来提速解码，是本题之外一个高级 serving 优化点。
浏览器 cookie 本身有大小上限也不该装用户隐私历史，拿它存完整聊天记录不是一个可行方向。
optionExplanations_en: Prompt and output safety review isn't part of this serving deep dive, but a real product can't ship without it — worth exploring separately.
Multi-GPU interconnect and model parallelism solve fitting a model too big for one card — a separate deep dive from this design's scheduling and fairness work.
Speculative decoding speeds up decoding by having a small model guess and the large model verify — an advanced serving optimization beyond this design.
A browser cookie has a hard size cap and shouldn't hold private chat history anyway — not a viable place to store full conversations.

scenario: ChatGPT 的 decode 阶段逐 token 串行，每次 GPU forward 都没吃满算力，要压每 token 延迟。
scenario_en: ChatGPT decodes one token at a time, leaving each GPU forward pass underused, and you need lower per-token latency.
q: speculative decoding 的核心思想是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea behind speculative decoding?
options: 用 Redis Pub/Sub 直接代替 GPU 计算
把用户的 prompt 拆分给多个数据库处理
先把所有回复内容写进 CDN 节点
小 draft model 先猜 token，大模型一次验证多个
why: decode 是逐 token 的瓶颈，draft model 猜得准时，大模型一次 forward 能确认多个后续 token。它是高级 serving 优化，不是基础 CRUD 能力。
why_en: Speculative decoding lets a small draft model propose tokens that the large model verifies in one step, improving decode throughput when guesses are right.
options_en: Use Redis Pub/Sub instead of a GPU.
Split the user prompt across multiple databases.
Write every reply to a CDN first.
A small draft model guesses several tokens and the big model verifies them in one pass.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用小模型猜测多个 token，让大模型一次验证以减少逐 token 解码次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Speculative decoding uses a small model to guess multiple tokens that the large model verifies in a single pass.

optionExplanations: Redis Pub/Sub 是消息广播工具，跟它有没有替代 GPU 计算完全不搭边。
把 prompt 拆给多个数据库处理，跟怎么加速逐 token 解码是两个不同层面的事。
先写 CDN 是内容分发层的优化，不解决 decode 阶段一步步生成 token 的瓶颈。
小 draft model 先便宜地猜出几个候选 token，大模型再一次 forward 同时验证它们，猜得准时能省下好几步逐 token 解码。
optionExplanations_en: Redis Pub/Sub is a broadcast tool — whether it 'replaces' a GPU has nothing to do with this.
Splitting the prompt across databases is a different layer of problem from speeding up token-by-token decoding.
Writing replies to a CDN first is a content-delivery optimization; it doesn't touch the decode-stage bottleneck.
A small draft model cheaply guesses several candidate tokens, and the large model verifies them all in one forward pass — when guesses land, it saves several steps of token-by-token decoding.

scenario: 部分 prompt 很简单，不需要最大模型；免费用户在高峰期也可以接受轻微质量降级来换取可用性和成本控制。
scenario_en: Some prompts are simple enough not to need the largest model, and free users can accept slight quality degradation at peak times for availability and cost control.
q: 哪种策略可以降低成本且通常不被用户明显感知？
q_en: Which strategy can lower cost without usually being obvious to users?
options: 路由简单请求到小模型，并缓存相似 prompt
所有请求永远使用最大模型处理
把所有 prompt 都延迟到夜间处理
直接删除掉历史上下文内容
why: 模型路由和语义缓存能减少昂贵模型调用，尤其适合简单或重复问题。它还可以和 tier 策略结合，让 free 流量先降级。
why_en: Routing simple prompts to cheaper models and caching semantically similar answers can cut cost without obvious user impact.
whenOtherWins: 高风险、复杂、付费或需要最高质量的请求仍应走强模型；个性化强的回复不适合缓存。
tradeoff: 路由 + 语义缓存降成本 vs 统一走最大模型
options_en: Route simple requests to a smaller model and cache semantically similar prompts.
Always use the largest model for every request.
Delay every prompt to be processed overnight.
Delete the conversation's history context.
optionExplanations: 简单或重复问题路由到小模型，再对相似 prompt 做语义缓存，能省下昂贵模型调用，且大多数用户根本感觉不出差异。
所有请求都走最大模型，成本最高也最不划算，跟“降成本”这个目标反着来。
把 prompt 都拖到夜里处理，用户等一整天才有回复，这是最容易被用户感知的降级方式。
直接删掉上下文会让模型明显“失忆”，用户一眼就能感知到，跟“不被明显感知”正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Routing simple or repeated prompts to a smaller model, plus caching semantically similar prompts, cuts calls to the expensive model, and most users can't tell the difference.
Always using the largest model is the most expensive option and works against the goal of cutting cost.
Delaying every prompt to overnight makes users wait a full day for a reply — about the most noticeable degradation possible.
Deleting context outright makes the model visibly 'forget,' something users notice immediately — the opposite of unobtrusive.

scenario: 用户希望 ChatGPT 记住几个月前另一个聊天里说过的偏好，而不只是本线程的旧轮。
scenario_en: A user expects ChatGPT to recall a preference stated months ago in a different chat, not just earlier turns of this thread.
q: 单对话 rolling summary 和跨聊天记忆的本质区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between single-chat rolling summary and cross-chat memory?
options: 两种记忆机制都只依赖浏览器本地缓存
单聊压缩旧轮，跨聊天用 embedding 检索
前者只能用于图片，后者只能用于文本
两者都要求使用强一致的分布式事务
why: 单对话记忆是把本线程旧内容折叠进 prompt；跨聊天记忆要从许多历史对话中找相关事实。后者更接近检索系统，而不是简单 summary。
why_en: Single-chat summaries compress one thread, while cross-chat memory is a retrieval problem over facts from many conversations.
tradeoff: 单对话摘要压缩 vs 跨对话检索
options_en: Both memory mechanisms rely only on browser-local cache.
Single-chat memory compresses old turns; cross-chat memory retrieves facts via embeddings.
The former only works for images, the latter only for text.
Both require the use of strongly consistent distributed transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本转成向量，用相似度检索相关内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding turns text into a vector so related content can be found by similarity.

optionExplanations: 两种记忆机制都只依赖浏览器本地缓存的说法站不住脚：跨聊天记忆需要服务端能查到别的对话，本地缓存看不到别的会话。
把这一条线程里的旧对话折叠压缩进 prompt 是单聊记忆的做法；跨聊天记忆则要从很多历史会话里找相关事实，靠的是 embedding 相似度检索，两种机制完全不同。
两种记忆机制处理的都是文本内容，跟是不是图片没有关系。
两者都要求使用强一致的分布式事务这个说法不成立：检索到的旧事实晚一点更新也不影响使用，最终一致就够了。
optionExplanations_en: Both memory mechanisms relying only on browser-local cache doesn't hold: cross-chat memory needs the server to see other conversations, which a local cache can't reach.

Single-chat memory folds old turns from this one thread into the prompt; cross-chat memory retrieves relevant facts from many past conversations via embedding similarity — a fundamentally different mechanism.
Both memory mechanisms operate on text content — being about images has nothing to do with it.
Both requiring strongly consistent distributed transactions doesn't hold either — a retrieved old fact updating slightly late doesn't break anything, eventual consistency is enough.

q: 把“低延迟且不断流”这一 marquee 决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the marquee decision chain for low latency and uninterrupted streaming in the right order:
steps: 选择 SSE 作为浏览器的单向 token 流
Redis Stream 按 runId 保存短期 delta 供重连补洞
需求：TTFT < 500ms 且流式输出平滑
成本：SSE 单向，取消要走 side-channel
worker 通过 XADD 写 delta，Chat Service XREAD 并转发
why: 先由用户体验确定推送，再由部署和重连问题引出 Redis Stream。取消 side-channel 是选择 SSE 后的可接受成本。
why_en: The streaming decision starts from low TTFT, chooses SSE, adds Redis Streams for reconnect replay, and accepts a side-channel for cancellation.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Need[Low perceived latency] --> SSE[SSE to browser]
SSE --> Stream[Redis Stream resume]
Stream --> Decouple[Decouple workers]
Decouple --> Backpressure[Bounded queue]

q: 把“GPU 受限容量”这一 marquee 决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the marquee decision chain for GPU-limited capacity in the right order:
steps: 用 bounded queue 和 admission control 给等待时间封顶
需求：20k prompts/sec 峰值且 GPU 昂贵稀缺
用 continuous batching 提高每个 worker 的 GPU 利用率
成本：调度层更复杂，还要定义容量不足时谁被拒绝
在 Chat Service 和 worker 之间放 pull-based queue
why: 先用队列隔离突刺，再用 backpressure 防止无限等待，最后用 continuous batching 榨干 GPU。复杂性主要转移到 serving scheduler 和产品降级策略。
why_en: The GPU-capacity chain adds a pull queue, bounded admission, and continuous batching, paying for more serving complexity.

q: 这个成本量级最直接支持哪个设计判断？
q_en: Which design call does this cost estimate support most directly?
options: GPU 成本可以忽略
只要买一台 GPU 就能服务 120k streams
推理账单可能达到每年数十亿美金量级，所以利用率优化值得投入
成本主要来自 Postgres 存储
why: 文章用公开报道的十亿美金级推理成本做现实锚点，说明每个百分点的 GPU 利用率都是真钱。continuous batching、backpressure 和路由都因此有价值。
why_en: Billion-dollar-scale inference spend makes GPU utilization improvements financially meaningful rather than premature optimization.
scenario: 公开报道显示 OpenAI 2024 年推理算力开销约 18 亿美金，且逐年上升到数十亿美金级。
scenario_en: Public reporting put OpenAI 2024 inference compute spend around 1.8 billion dollars, rising toward multi-billion-dollar annual costs.
options_en: GPU cost can be ignored.
One GPU is enough to serve 120k concurrent streams.
Inference bills can reach billions of dollars a year, so utilization work is worth it.
Cost mainly comes from Postgres storage.
optionExplanations: 十亿美金级别的账单摆在那，说 GPU 成本可以忽略明显与现实报道矛盾。
一台 GPU 撑起 120k 并发流远超单卡算力和显存上限，这是不可能的假设。
公开报道显示推理算力开销已经到十亿美金级别，意味着哪怕一个百分点的利用率提升都是真金白银，批处理调度、过载保护和智能路由这些工程投入才划算。
聊天记录这种简单行存储的 Postgres 开销和 GPU 推理账单完全不是一个数量级，成本大头显然不在这里。
optionExplanations_en: With a billion-dollar-scale bill on record, calling GPU cost ignorable directly contradicts the reported numbers.
One GPU serving 120k concurrent streams far exceeds any single card's compute and memory limits — not a realistic assumption.

Public reporting puts inference compute spend at a billion-dollar scale, meaning even a single point of utilization gain is real money — that's what justifies investing in continuous batching, backpressure, and routing.
Postgres cost for simple chat rows is nowhere near the scale of the GPU inference bill — the cost clearly isn't concentrated there.

scenario: 面试官在评 mid-level：同步 MVP 会让用户盯 30 秒空白屏，看候选人能否自己发现。
scenario_en: The interviewer is calibrating a mid-level candidate: the synchronous MVP leaves a 30-second blank screen, and they watch who spots it.
q: 中级候选人在这题里至少应主动识别什么问题？
q_en: What issue should a mid-level candidate at least identify in this design?
options: 必须能证明 Redis Stream 的内部源码实现
必须完整实现 speculative decoding 算法
必须设计完整的多模态 tokenization 方案
识别 30 秒空白屏问题，知道要 streaming 和排队
why: 中级期望是清楚 API、数据模型和同步 MVP，并能在提示下或主动看到 streaming 与队列。更深的 continuous batching、prefix cache 属于更高层级加分。
why_en: A mid-level answer should recognize that blank-screen synchronous generation needs streaming and that GPU work needs a queue.
options_en: Prove out the internal source of Redis Streams.
Fully implement speculative decoding.
Design a complete multimodal tokenization scheme.
Recognize the 30-second blank-screen problem and know it needs streaming plus a queue.
optionExplanations: 背出 Redis Stream 的内部源码实现属于系统内部实现细节，不是中级候选人的预期门槛。
完整实现 speculative decoding 算法是很深的推理优化，超出中级水平通常要求的深度。
设计完整的多模态 tokenization 方案同样是加分项而非中级基础门槛。
至少要能看出同步 MVP 会让用户盯着 30 秒空白屏，并且知道要靠 streaming 和排队来解决，这是中级候选人该主动识别的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Reciting Redis Streams' internal source implementation is internal-implementation trivia, not what a mid-level candidate is expected to know.
Fully implementing speculative decoding is deep inference optimization, well beyond typical mid-level depth.
Designing a complete multimodal tokenization scheme is likewise a bonus, not a mid-level baseline.
At minimum, spotting that the synchronous MVP leaves users staring at a 30-second blank screen, and knowing it needs streaming plus a queue, is what a mid-level candidate should surface on their own.

scenario: 面试官在评 senior：高层设计半小时内就该过完，剩下的时间看深度落在哪一块。
scenario_en: The interviewer is calibrating a senior candidate: the high-level design should be done in half an hour, then depth decides the signal.
q: Senior 候选人的重点深度通常落在哪里？
q_en: Where should a senior candidate usually go deep in this design?
options: SSE vs WebSocket、GPU 调度与成本
只画一张普通的 REST CRUD 流程图
只讨论前端界面的 UI 文案细节
只讨论数据库表结构的范式设计
why: Senior 要快速过高层设计，把时间放在流式 fanout、GPU 调度、公平性和上下文成本。能讲清协议与调度取舍是关键。
why_en: Senior candidates should move quickly into streaming fanout, GPU scheduling, fairness, and context-cost trade-offs.
options_en: SSE vs WebSocket, GPU scheduling, and long-conversation cost control.
Draw only one plain REST CRUD flow diagram.
Discuss only the frontend interface's UI copy.
Discuss only database table-schema normalization.
optionExplanations: SSE vs WebSocket 的协议取舍、GPU 调度和长对话成本控制，正是这题真正的难点所在，senior 应该把时间砸在这里。
只画一张普通的 REST CRUD 流程图停在功能性设计，完全没碰到延迟、并发和成本这些非功能要求。
只讨论前端界面的 UI 文案细节不是这道系统设计题的技术评分点，纠结这个是跑偏了。
只讨论数据库表结构的范式设计不是本题的核心难点，聊天记录的数据模型本身很简单。
optionExplanations_en: The SSE-vs-WebSocket trade-off, GPU scheduling, and long-conversation cost control are exactly where this question gets hard — a senior candidate should spend time there.
Drawing just one plain REST CRUD flow diagram stops at functional design and never touches latency, concurrency, or cost — the non-functional asks.
Discussing only the frontend interface's UI copy isn't what this system-design question grades — dwelling there misses the point.
Discussing only database table-schema normalization isn't the hard part here; the chat data model itself is simple.

scenario: 面试官在评 Staff+：模板化的高层设计谁都会画，区分度只剩深度之间的串联。
scenario_en: The interviewer is calibrating Staff-plus: anyone can draw the templated high-level design, so only connected depth separates answers.
q: Staff+ 答案区别于普通答案的标志是什么？
q_en: What marks a Staff+ answer as different from a standard answer?
options: 只是简单罗列出更多个数据库产品的名字而已
把 GPU 经济性、调度、公平和降级串成一个整体
刻意回避掉整个数字估算推导的过程
把强一致性直接当成这道题默认的设计目标
why: Staff+ 需要带来超出模板的 serving 深度，尤其是 GPU 成本、推理内部优化和降级策略之间的连接。文章明确提到 speculative decoding 等知识也逐渐成为常识。
why_en: A staff-level answer connects GPU economics, batching, KV-cache reuse, tiered fairness, and graceful degradation into one serving architecture.
options_en: Just simply list out a few more database product names.
Weave GPU economics, scheduling, fairness, and degradation into one coherent story.
Deliberately avoid going through the whole numeric estimation process.
Treat strong consistency directly as this question's default design goal.
optionExplanations: 只是罗列出更多数据库产品的名字只是知识面广，不代表能把系统串成一个连贯的整体判断。
把 GPU 经济性、调度、公平和降级策略这些独立的点串成一个互相牵引的整体故事，这才是超出模板答案的深度。
刻意回避掉任何数字估算的过程反而是缺陷，staff 级别恰恰需要用量级去支撑判断，而不是绕开它。
把强一致性直接当成默认的设计目标违背了这道题“可用性优先”的判断，属于方向性错误而非加分项。
optionExplanations_en: Just listing out more database product names shows breadth, not tying the system into one coherent judgment.
Weaving GPU economics, scheduling, fairness, and degradation into one story that pulls together is exactly what goes beyond a templated answer.
Deliberately avoiding going through any numeric estimation is actually a weakness — staff level is supposed to back judgment with magnitude, not dodge it.
Treating strong consistency directly as the default design goal contradicts this design's availability-first call — a directional mistake, not a plus.

scenario: 从同步阻塞 MVP 出发，要撑住 120k 并发流、固定 GPU 容量和长对话的上下文成本。
scenario_en: Starting from a synchronous blocking MVP, the design must carry 120k concurrent streams, fixed GPU capacity and long-chat context cost.
q: 最终设计相比同步 MVP 增加了哪些关键组件？（多选）
q_en: Which key components does the final design add beyond the synchronous MVP? (Choose all that apply.)
options: SSE + Redis Stream 的 runId token 流
bounded queue、admission control 和 continuous batching worker
per-user token budgets 与 tier-aware priority queue
把每个 token 永久写入数据库作为唯一真相
why: 最终架构补上了 streaming、GPU 调度公平、上下文成本三块；每 token 落库仍不在范围内，只持久化最终 assistant message。
why_en: The final architecture adds resumable streaming, bounded GPU scheduling with batching, and cost-aware tiered fairness, not durable storage for every token.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] -->|POST prompt| Chat[Chat Service]
Client -->|SSE runId| Chat
Chat --> DB[(Postgres)]
Chat --> Queue[Bounded Queue]
Worker[GPU Workers] -->|XADD deltas| Stream[(Redis Stream)]
Chat -->|XREAD| Stream
Queue --> Worker
options_en: An SSE plus Redis Stream token flow keyed by runId.
A bounded queue with admission control and continuous-batching workers.
Per-user token budgets plus a tier-aware priority queue.
Permanently writing every token to the database as the source of truth.
optionExplanations: SSE 加按 runId 建的 Redis Stream，同时解决了低 TTFT 推送和断线重连补洞两个问题。
bounded queue、admission control 和 continuous batching worker 一起处理 GPU 调度、过载保护和利用率。
per-user token budgets 和 tier-aware 优先队列分别解决公平性和付费用户优先级。
把每个 token 永久写数据库违反了“只持久化最终消息”的范围设定，最终架构并没有采用这条路。
optionExplanations_en: SSE plus a runId-keyed Redis Stream solves both low-TTFT delivery and gap-free reconnect replay.
A bounded queue, admission control, and continuous-batching workers together handle GPU scheduling, overload protection, and utilization.
Per-user token budgets and a tier-aware priority queue separately cover fairness and paid-tier priority.
Permanently writing every token to a database breaks the 'persist only the final message' scope — the final architecture never adopted this path.

scenario: 120k 并发生成各自有一条按 runId 建的 Redis Stream 存 token delta，只用于断线重放，最终 assistant message 落 Postgres。
scenario_en: Each of 120k concurrent generations has its own runId-keyed Redis Stream holding token deltas purely for reconnect replay; the final assistant message lands in Postgres.
q: 这些 runId Stream 靠什么让 Redis 内存封顶？
q_en: What keeps the memory used by these runId streams bounded in Redis?
options: XADD 时带 MAXLEN 截断，并给 stream 设一个短 TTL
不设上限，靠 Redis 的全局淘汰策略在内存满时自己踢
每条 delta 同步写一份到 Postgres，Redis 里只留指针
Chat Service 每读完一条就 XDEL，把 stream 当一次性队列消费掉
options_en: XADD with MAXLEN truncation plus a short TTL on each stream.
No cap at all — let global Redis eviction drop keys when memory fills up.
Mirror every delta into Postgres and keep only a pointer in Redis.
Have Chat Service XDEL each entry after reading it, draining the stream like a queue.
optionExplanations: MAXLEN 限住单条流的长度，TTL 限住它的存活时间，两个上限合起来内存才封顶。
全局淘汰会在内存吃紧时随机踢掉正在被重放的流，重连补洞直接失败。
每 token 落库正是被划在范围外的 per-token 持久化，一次回答变成几千次小写入。
读完即删只服务当下那一个消费者；客户端换实例重连后已经没有条目可以重放了。
optionExplanations_en: MAXLEN caps how long one stream gets, TTL caps how long it lives — together they bound memory.
Global eviction can drop a stream that a client is still replaying, so gap-filling fails.
Persisting every token is the per-token durability we put below the line; one answer becomes thousands of tiny writes.
