Deleting on read serves only the consumer present right then; a client that reconnects elsewhere has nothing left to replay.
why: Stream 是短期工作态而不是第二份历史：MAXLEN 只留最近一段窗口、TTL 让生成结束后回收，内存才随并发数封顶。代价是超出窗口的重连补不回来，只能等完成后从 Postgres 重取。
why_en: The stream is short-lived working state, not a second copy of history — MAXLEN plus a short TTL cap memory, at the cost of a reconnect older than the window falling back to refetching from Postgres.
tradeoff: 内存封顶 vs 可重放窗口的长度
whenOtherWins: 如果重放窗口必须覆盖整段 30 秒回答，就把 MAXLEN 调大并接受更高的常驻内存。
codeSample:
XADD gen:{runId} MAXLEN ~ 2000 * delta "hello"
EXPIRE gen:{runId} 300

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis XADD 的截断参数，限制一条 stream 最多保留多少条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAXLEN is the XADD argument that caps how many entries a Redis stream keeps.

termDefinitions.meaning: 键的存活时间，到点后 Redis 自动删除这个 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the lifetime after which Redis automatically deletes a key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往 Redis Stream 末尾追加一条记录的命令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XADD appends one entry to the end of a Redis stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按条目 ID 删除 Redis Stream 里某条记录的命令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XDEL removes a specific entry from a Redis stream by its ID.

termDefinitions.meaning: 增量：这里指单个新生成的 token，而不是到目前为止的整段文本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delta here is a single newly generated token rather than the whole text so far.

scenario: 多轮对话每轮的 prompt 前缀几乎不变，worker 能缓存这段前缀的 KV cache；调度器目前把每次请求随手发给任意空闲 worker。
scenario_en: Across turns the prompt prefix barely changes and a worker can keep its KV cache warm, but the scheduler currently hands each request to any idle worker.
q: 要让 prefix caching 真的省下钱，调度还得配合做什么？
q_en: What must the scheduler also do for prefix caching to actually save money?
options: 把同一 chat 的后续轮次尽量送回前缀已热的那个 worker
让每个 worker 都保存全部对话的前缀，用复制换命中率
把 KV cache 集中放进一个共享 Redis，供所有 worker 随取随用
把 batch 开得更大，让更多序列进入同一次 forward pass
options_en: Route later turns of one chat back to the worker whose prefix is already warm.
Have every worker keep every conversation prefix, trading replication for hit rate.
Put the KV cache in one shared Redis so any worker can pull it on demand.
Raise batch size so more sequences ride the same forward pass.
optionExplanations: 缓存是每台 worker 本地的，命中只发生在同一台机器上，路由必须带一点粘性。
把每段前缀复制到所有 worker，显存开销乘以机器数，反而更早触发驱逐。
KV cache 是显存里的中间张量，搬到远端 Redis 的传输成本比重算还高。
大 batch 提升的是吞吐，不会让某台 worker 恰好持有这段对话的前缀。
optionExplanations_en: The cache is local to each worker, so a hit only happens on the same machine — routing needs some stickiness.
Replicating every prefix to every worker multiplies memory use and triggers eviction sooner.
The KV cache is intermediate tensors in GPU memory; shipping them to remote Redis costs more than recomputing.
Bigger batches raise throughput but do nothing to put this conversation on a worker that already holds its prefix.
why: 前缀缓存只在命中时省钱，请求散开就没有一台 worker 保持热前缀，每轮都要全价重算。代价是路由带上粘性，负载均衡和故障转移的自由度变小。
why_en: Prefix caching only pays off on a hit, so turns of one conversation have to land on the same warm worker — the price is stickier routing and less freedom to balance load.
tradeoff: 缓存命中率 vs 调度自由度
whenOtherWins: 如果对话轮次间隔很久、前缀早被驱逐，粘性只会制造热点，不如按负载自由派发。

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型处理 prompt 时算出的中间注意力状态，缓存下来可以跳过重复计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The KV cache is the intermediate attention state a model computes for a prompt, reusable to skip recomputation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 prompt 中稳定不变的前缀部分的中间状态缓存起来复用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prefix caching reuses the cached model state for the stable leading part of a prompt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型的一次前向计算，在解码阶段对应产出一个 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A forward pass is one pass through the model, producing one token during decoding.

scenario: worker 显存只够同时保住有限几个对话的前缀 KV cache，按 LRU 驱逐。用户中午聊完，晚上回来接着聊同一个 chat。
scenario_en: A worker has room for only a limited number of warm prefix KV caches and evicts them LRU-style; a user chats at noon and returns to the same chat at night.
q: 晚上这一轮请求要多付出什么？
q_en: What does that evening turn end up paying for?
options: 前缀已被驱逐，这一轮要全价重算前缀，TTFT 明显变高
中午说过的内容已经丢失，模型看不到那段历史了
这一轮会被直接拒绝，用户必须新开一个 chat 才能继续
只要 Postgres 里还留着消息，前缀就一定还在显存里等着
options_en: The prefix was evicted, so this turn re-runs the full prefill and TTFT jumps.
The noon messages are gone and the model can no longer see that history.
The turn is rejected outright and the user has to start a fresh chat.
As long as the messages are in Postgres, the prefix is still sitting in GPU memory.
optionExplanations: 驱逐掉的是算好的中间状态，不是内容；重建它就是把整段历史重新前向一遍。
历史存在 Postgres 里，永远拼得回 prompt，冷掉的只是加速用的缓存。
缓存未命中从来不是拒绝理由，它只影响这一轮的延迟和成本。
落库和显存是两套存储，消息还在不代表显存里的前缀还没被 LRU 挤掉。
optionExplanations_en: What gets evicted is precomputed state, not content — rebuilding it means running the whole history forward again.
History lives in Postgres and can always be reassembled; only the accelerating cache went cold.
A cache miss is never grounds for rejection — it only affects this turn's latency and cost.
Durable rows and GPU memory are different stores; a persisted message says nothing about the prefix surviving LRU.
why: 命中时可以跳过 prefill 直接出 token；对话变冷后 LRU 把前缀挤出显存，下一轮只能把全部历史重新前向一遍才开始生成。丢的是中间状态，不是内容。
why_en: A warm hit skips prefill entirely, but once LRU evicts a quiet conversation the next turn re-runs the whole history through the model first — what was lost is computed state, not content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种驱逐策略：内存不够时先踢掉最久没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU is an eviction policy that discards the entry untouched for the longest time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成第一个 token 之前，把整段输入 prompt 前向计算一遍的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prefill is the phase that runs the whole input prompt through the model before the first output token.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户按下回车到屏幕上出现第一个 token 的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTFT is the time from hitting enter to the first token appearing on screen.

scenario: 前沿模型的权重放不进单张 GPU，要拆到一整箱 GPU 上；题目给定的并发假设是约 120k 条同时在生成的流（这是给定前提，不是算出来的）。
scenario_en: A frontier model's weights do not fit on one GPU and must be split across a whole box; the given assumption is about 120k concurrent in-flight streams (a premise, not a derived figure).
q: 由此推出的 GPU 规模量级支撑哪个判断？
q_en: Which judgement does the resulting GPU fleet size support?
options: 数万张 GPU 量级，利用率每一个百分点都是真金白银
几百张 GPU 就够，调度和批处理都可以先不做
GPU 数量只由 200M DAU 决定，与并发流条数无关
只要模型足够小，单张 GPU 就能服务掉全部并发流
options_en: Tens of thousands of GPUs, where every point of utilization is real money.
A few hundred GPUs is enough, so scheduling and batching can wait.
Fleet size follows the 200M DAU figure and not the concurrent-stream count.
With a small enough model a single GPU could serve all concurrent streams.
optionExplanations: 成千上万个箱子 × 每箱多张卡，账单大到足以为调度上的每一分工程投入买单。
几百张卡撑不住 120k 条同时解码的序列，这个估算的意义正是排除这种直觉。
DAU 决定一天的总请求量，决定机队规模的是同一时刻在跑的流数。
题目设定就是权重放不进单卡，所以"单卡服务全部"从前提上就不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Thousands of boxes times several cards each produces a bill large enough to justify every scheduling optimization.
A few hundred cards cannot carry 120k sequences decoding at once — ruling that out is the point of the estimate.
DAU sets daily request volume; fleet size follows how many streams run at the same instant.
The premise is that the weights do not fit on one card, so one GPU serving everything is ruled out up front.
why: 并发流数 ÷ 每箱能同时承载的流数 × 每箱 GPU 数：120k 条流要成千上万个箱子，落在数万张 GPU 的量级。这个数字是后面 continuous batching 和 backpressure 值不值得做的成本依据。
why_en: Concurrent streams divided by streams per box, times GPUs per box, puts 120k streams at tens of thousands of GPUs — the number that justifies spending on batching and backpressure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器，这里指跑大模型推理的加速卡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU is the accelerator card that runs large-model inference here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数，衡量每天有多少用户使用产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU is the number of unique users active on a given day.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让序列随时进出同一个运行中的批，批一有空位就补上新请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous batching lets sequences enter and leave a running batch so a freed slot is refilled immediately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 背压：下游忙不过来时主动限入或拒绝，避免排队无限增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure means rejecting or deferring work when downstream is saturated, so queues cannot grow without bound.

scenario: 高级设计每轮都把完整历史拼进 prompt。一段 50 轮的对话平均每轮约 500 token，输入 token 按每次调用计费。
scenario_en: The high-level design replays the whole conversation each turn; a 50-turn chat averages about 500 tokens per turn and input tokens are billed per call.
q: 下一轮 prompt 的输入规模是多大，说明什么？
q_en: How large is the next prompt, and what does that imply?
options: 约 25k 输入 token，且每轮继续涨，必须做截断或摘要
始终 500 输入 token，与对话已经进行了多少轮无关
25k 是输出 token 量，成本压力其实落在解码那一侧
输入量恒定不变，只有回答变长才会推高这次调用的成本
options_en: About 25k input tokens, still growing each turn, so truncation or summarization is required.
A flat 500 input tokens regardless of how many turns have happened.
The 25k figure is output tokens, so the cost pressure sits on the decode side.
Input size stays constant and only longer answers raise the cost of a call.
optionExplanations: 每轮都重放全部历史，所以输入量随轮数线性累积，这是压缩手段的成本基线。
只发最新一句就没有上下文了，模型会立刻显得完全不记得前面聊过什么。
重放历史撑大的是输入侧；输出长度由回答本身决定，不随对话变长。
"输入恒定"正是最常见的误判，它会让人以为长对话不需要任何成本治理。
optionExplanations_en: Replaying full history makes input grow linearly with turns — this is the baseline every compression lever is measured against.
Sending only the newest message drops the context and the assistant instantly looks amnesiac.
Replaying history inflates the input side; output length is set by the answer itself, not by chat age.
Assuming constant input is the classic misread that makes long chats look free.
why: 50 轮 × 每轮约 500 token ≈ 25k 输入 token（token 是模型处理文本的最小单位），而且还在逐轮累加。它是判断截断、rolling summary、prefix caching 值不值得的成本基线。
why_en: Fifty turns at roughly five hundred tokens each is about twenty-five thousand input tokens and still climbing, which is the cost baseline that justifies truncation, summaries and prefix caching.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型处理文本的最小单位，大致相当于一个词或词的一部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest unit of text a model processes, roughly a word or word piece.

termDefinitions.meaning: 滚动摘要：把较老的对话轮次压缩成一段摘要，最近几轮保留原文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rolling summary compresses older turns into a running summary while keeping recent turns verbatim.

scenario: GPU worker 生成一段回答要 30 秒。Chat Service 通过 gRPC 调 worker，再把 token 转发到浏览器的 SSE 连接上。
scenario_en: A worker takes 30 seconds to generate an answer; Chat Service calls it over gRPC and relays tokens down the browser's SSE connection.
q: 这个内部调用若用普通一问一答而非 server-streaming，用户看到什么？
q_en: If that internal call were plain request/response instead of server-streaming, what would the user see?
options: worker 攒满整段才返回，浏览器又空屏 30 秒
token 会乱序到达浏览器，客户端必须按序号自己重新排好
SSE 连接会被判定为超时断开，客户端不停地发起重连
TTFT 不变，只是整段回答的总完成时间被明显拉长
options_en: The worker buffers the whole completion, so the browser is blank for 30 seconds again.
Tokens arrive out of order and the client has to reorder them by sequence number.
The SSE connection times out and the client keeps reconnecting.
TTFT is unchanged and only total completion time gets longer.
optionExplanations: worker 没有中途交付的机会，只能把结果攒齐后一次性交回。
乱序是多连接并发才有的问题；单条流本身就是有序的，换成一问一答也不会乱。
超时是可能的副作用，但不是这里的核心失败；核心是首 token 根本推不出来。
恰恰相反：受损的是 TTFT，总生成时间基本不变，因为模型的活儿一样多。
optionExplanations_en: The worker gets no chance to deliver partway; it can only hand back the finished result in one lump.
Out-of-order delivery is a multi-connection problem; a single stream is ordered either way.
A timeout is a possible side effect but not the core failure — the point is the first token never gets out.
It is the reverse: TTFT is what breaks, while total generation time stays about the same.
why: 一问一答会把 token 全压在 worker 缓冲里直到生成结束，TTFT 退回整整 30 秒，正是空屏问题重演。流式的代价是两端都要处理半截响应。
why_en: A plain call forces the worker to buffer the whole completion, pushing time-to-first-token back to the full thirty seconds — the blank-screen problem again, and streaming costs both sides handling partial responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跑在 HTTP/2 上的服务间调用框架，支持一次调用返回一串消息的 server-streaming。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a service-to-service RPC framework over HTTP/2 that supports server-streaming replies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览器通过一条普通 HTTP 连接单向接收服务端持续推送的事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a browser receive a one-way stream of server pushes over a plain HTTP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户按下回车到屏幕上出现第一个 token 的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTFT is the time from hitting enter to the first token appearing on screen.

scenario: 假设坚持用每几百毫秒轮询一次来取新 token，那么 worker 产出的 token 必须先落在一个被轮询的接口能读到的地方。
scenario_en: If we insist on polling every few hundred milliseconds, the tokens a worker produces must first land somewhere the polled endpoint can read.
q: 把这个中间 buffer 放 Postgres，代价具体是什么？
q_en: If that intermediate buffer is Postgres, what exactly does it cost?
options: 一次回答被拆成几百次小写入，全部打在系统记录库上
Postgres 读不到 worker 刚写的行，必须先等主从同步完成
token 的先后顺序无法保证，还要额外维护一列序号
Postgres 存不了文本增量，只能存整段已完成的消息
options_en: One answer becomes hundreds of tiny writes, all aimed at the system of record.
Postgres cannot read the row the worker just wrote until replication catches up.
Token ordering is not guaranteed and needs an extra sequence column.
Postgres cannot store text deltas, only whole finished messages.
optionExplanations: 每个 token 一行，120k 并发流会把写放大直接压到我们最不该压的那台库上。
同库读写没有这个问题；副本延迟是另一个话题，不是这里的代价。
写入时带自增主键顺序天然有保证，排序不是这条路的痛点。
存一行短文本对关系库毫无难度，问题在写入次数而不是能不能存。
optionExplanations_en: One row per token means 120k concurrent streams hammer write amplification into the one database we least want to stress.
Reading your own write in the same database is fine; replica lag is a different topic.
An auto-increment key gives ordering for free, so ordering is not the pain here.
Storing a short text row is trivial for a relational store — the problem is the number of writes.
why: 轮询要求 token 先落地：Redis 快但一重启整段回放就没了，Postgres 持久却把一次回答变成几百次小写入压在系统记录库上。两条路都不好，才逼出服务端推送。
why_en: Polling forces the tokens to land somewhere first — Redis is fast but loses everything on restart, Postgres is durable but turns one answer into hundreds of tiny writes against the system of record.

rows: 每 token 一行，写放大

termDefinitions.meaning: system of record，存放业务真相的那份主数据库，这里是 Postgres。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The system of record is the authoritative database holding business truth — Postgres here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑操作被展开成远多于一次的物理写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification is when one logical operation expands into many physical writes.

scenario: 浏览器对同一域名的 HTTP/1.1 并发连接上限是 6 条，而一个用户可能同时开着好几个标签页，每页都挂着一条 SSE 长连接。
scenario_en: Browsers cap HTTP/1.1 connections per domain at six, and one user may keep several tabs open, each holding an SSE connection.
q: 这个连接配额对 SSE 方案有多严重？
q_en: How serious is that connection quota for the SSE design?
options: 确实吃掉那 6 条配额，但升到 HTTP/2 多路复用后就不成问题
确实吃掉配额，而且 HTTP/2 也救不了，只能改用 WebSocket
完全不占配额，SSE 走的是独立于 HTTP 的另一套连接池
只在服务端占资源，浏览器一侧根本没有任何并发上限
options_en: It really does consume the six-connection budget, but HTTP/2 multiplexing removes the issue.
It consumes the budget and HTTP/2 cannot help, so WebSocket is the only way out.
It costs nothing — SSE uses a separate connection pool outside HTTP.
It only costs server resources; browsers impose no per-domain concurrency limit at all.
optionExplanations: 长连接一直挂着不释放，所以在 HTTP/1.1 下它是实打实占用名额的。
HTTP/2 把所有请求复用进一条连接，配额问题正好在这里消失，不必换协议。
SSE 就是一个一直不结束的普通 HTTP 响应，用的正是同一个连接池。
每域名并发上限是浏览器侧的老规矩，服务端资源是另一回事。
optionExplanations_en: A long-lived connection never releases its slot, so under HTTP/1.1 it genuinely occupies one.
HTTP/2 multiplexes everything onto one connection, which is exactly where the quota problem disappears.
SSE is just an ordinary HTTP response that never ends, using the very same connection pool.
The per-domain limit is a browser-side rule; server resources are a separate question.
why: SSE 是长期挂住的普通 HTTP 响应，在 HTTP/1.1 下真会占掉每域 6 条名额；HTTP/2 多路复用把它们并到一条连接上，限制就消失。代价是整条链路（LB、代理）都得支持 HTTP/2。
why_en: SSE holds an ordinary HTTP response open, so it really does eat the six-per-domain budget on HTTP/1.1, while HTTP/2 multiplexing dissolves the limit — provided every proxy on the path speaks it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览器通过一条普通 HTTP 连接单向接收服务端持续推送的事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a browser receive a one-way stream of server pushes over a plain HTTP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 的第二版，可以把多个请求多路复用到同一条 TCP 连接上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 multiplexes many requests onto a single TCP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条全双工长连接，客户端和服务端都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a full-duplex persistent connection where both sides can send at any time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多条逻辑流共用一条物理连接，互不阻塞地交错传输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multiplexing interleaves several logical streams over one physical connection.

scenario: 还没有队列，Chat Service 直接把请求丢给某个 GPU worker。此刻有人提交了一个 30k token 的超长 prompt。
scenario_en: With no queue yet, Chat Service hands each request straight to a GPU worker — and someone just submitted a 30k-token prompt.
q: 直连 worker 时这条超长请求会对后面的短请求做什么？
q_en: With direct dispatch, what does that huge request do to the short ones behind it?
options: 它独占那台 worker，后面的短请求全被堵在队首干等
短请求会被自动改派到别的空闲 worker，基本不受影响
长 prompt 会被自动拆成几段，与短请求交替着执行
短请求先被处理，长 prompt 排到最后，整体延迟其实不变
options_en: It monopolizes that worker while short requests sit stuck behind it.
Short requests get rerouted to other idle workers and barely notice.
The long prompt is split into chunks that interleave with short requests.
Short requests go first, the long prompt goes last, and overall latency is unchanged.
optionExplanations: 谁先到谁占住，一条超长请求就把后面一串短请求锁死在队首。
没有调度器就没人知道哪台有余量，改派要么不存在要么是自己造的劣质旁路。
拆分需要调度器介入；直连模式下 worker 只知道埋头做完手上这条。
"先做短的"正是需要优先级调度才有的行为，直连模式给不了。
optionExplanations_en: First come, first served means one huge request locks a queue of short ones behind it.
Without a scheduler nobody knows which worker has room, so rerouting either does not exist or is a bad homegrown side channel.
Splitting requires a scheduler; with direct dispatch the worker just finishes what it holds.
Serving short requests first is exactly the behaviour priority scheduling buys, and direct dispatch has none.
why: 没有队列和调度时是谁先到谁占住 worker，一条 30k token 的 prompt 就把后面的短请求锁在队首，延迟变得完全不可预测。队列加 continuous batching 才让短请求能挤进同一批。
why_en: Without a queue it is first-come-first-served on the worker, so one huge prompt blocks the short requests behind it and latency becomes unpredictable until batching lets them share a batch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 队首的一个慢任务把后面所有任务一起拖住的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Head-of-line blocking is when one slow item at the front of a queue stalls everything behind it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让序列随时进出同一个运行中的批，批一有空位就补上新请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous batching lets sequences enter and leave a running batch so a freed slot is refilled immediately.

diagram:
flowchart LR
Long[30k token 长请求] --> W[GPU Worker]
S1[短请求 1] -->|排队等待| W
S2[短请求 2] -->|排队等待| W
W --> Out[30 秒后才轮到短请求]

scenario: 一个批里既有一句话的回复，也有 2000 token 的长文；GPU 每次 forward pass 把批内所有序列各推进一个 token。
scenario_en: One batch holds both a one-line reply and a 2000-token essay, and each forward pass advances every sequence in the batch by one token.
q: 固定 batch 在这种长度参差下怎么退化？
q_en: How does a fixed batch degrade when sequence lengths differ this much?
options: 短序列做完后位置空着，整批要等最慢那条，GPU 漂回空闲
短序列会被提前踢出并重新排队，已经生成的 token 全部作废
长序列被截断到批内最短的那个长度，答案变得不完整
固定 batch 利用率反而更高，因为批大小不变、调度也最简单
options_en: Finished short sequences leave empty slots while the batch waits for the slowest one, and the GPU drifts back to idle.
Short sequences get evicted and requeued, throwing away the tokens already generated.
Long sequences are truncated to the shortest length in the batch, so answers come out incomplete.
A fixed batch actually gets better utilization because the batch size never changes and scheduling is simplest.
optionExplanations: 批要整体排空才能换下一批，所以空出来的槽位在最慢序列跑完前一直闲着。
踢掉进行中的序列会浪费已算的状态，没有 serving 框架会这么做。
批不会改写生成长度，每条序列各自生成到自己的结束条件为止。
简单是真的，但代价正是这些空槽，利用率恰恰输给会补位的批策略。
optionExplanations_en: A fixed batch must drain fully before the next one starts, so freed slots idle until the slowest sequence ends.
Evicting a running sequence would throw away computed state; no serving framework does that.
Batching does not rewrite generation length — each sequence runs to its own stop condition.
It is simpler, but those empty slots are the price, and utilization loses to a policy that refills freed slots.
why: 固定 batch 要等整批排空才换下一批，一条 2000 token 的长文会让旁边做完的槽位一直空转；continuous batching 一完成就立刻塞进队列里的下一条，把批填满。
why_en: A fixed batch waits for its slowest sequence before starting the next one, leaving finished slots idle, while continuous batching drops a sequence the moment it ends and slots in a queued request.
tradeoff: GPU 利用率 vs serving 层调度复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型的一次前向计算，在解码阶段对应产出一个 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A forward pass is one pass through the model, producing one token during decoding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让序列随时进出同一个运行中的批，批一有空位就补上新请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous batching lets sequences enter and leave a running batch so a freed slot is refilled immediately.

scenario: worker 从"一次跑一条 prompt"改成 continuous batching：序列随时进出同一个正在运行的批。
scenario_en: Workers move from running one prompt at a time to continuous batching, with sequences entering and leaving a running batch.
q: 改用 continuous batching 后 serving 层多付出什么？
q_en: What does the serving layer pay for continuous batching?
options: 要管理变长序列随时进出批，且长度参差时仍留有 GPU 空闲
必须放弃流式输出，只能等整批算完再整段返回给用户
显存占用被固定死，吞吐反而低于一次只跑一条的做法
需要把批内所有 prompt 先补齐到相同长度才允许它们进批
options_en: It must juggle variable-length sequences entering and leaving, and uneven lengths still leave some GPU idle.
It has to give up streaming and return the whole answer once the batch finishes.
Memory use is pinned and throughput drops below running one sequence at a time.
Every prompt in the batch must first be padded to the same length before it can join.
optionExplanations: 批不再是一个静态集合，worker 实际上变成了一个要不断增删成员的小调度器。
批处理和流式并不冲突，每次 forward pass 产出的 token 照样立刻推出去。
提高吞吐正是批处理的目的；说它更慢就把这条杠杆的动机整个搞反了。
补齐长度是固定批的老做法，continuous batching 要解决的恰恰是长度不齐。
optionExplanations_en: The batch stops being a static set — the worker effectively becomes a small scheduler adding and removing members.
Batching and streaming coexist: each forward pass still pushes its tokens out immediately.
Higher throughput is the whole point; claiming it is slower inverts the motivation for the lever.
Padding to equal length is the fixed-batch habit that continuous batching exists to avoid.
why: 收益是 GPU 少空转，代价是 worker 从"跑一条 prompt"变成要处理变长序列进出的调度器，而且 prompt 长度差异大时批内仍有算力浪费。多数复杂度由推理框架替你扛。
why_en: The GPU idles less, but the worker turns from a single-prompt runner into a scheduler juggling variable-length sequences, and wildly uneven prompts still waste some compute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让序列随时进出同一个运行中的批，批一有空位就补上新请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous batching lets sequences enter and leave a running batch so a freed slot is refilled immediately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型服务层：负责收请求、组批、调度 GPU 并把 token 吐回去的那层软件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving layer accepts requests, forms batches, schedules GPUs and streams tokens back.

scenario: Chat Service 是无状态、横向扩容的，要给每个用户加配额，任何一台实例都必须看到同一份计数。
scenario_en: Chat Service is stateless and horizontally scaled, so any instance enforcing a per-user quota must see the same counter.
q: 这个限流计数器该放哪、怎么判？
q_en: Where should that rate-limit counter live, and how is it checked?
options: 计数放 Redis，做原子 incr-and-check，超限直接返回 429
每台实例各自在内存里计数，把限额除以实例数凑出来
计数写 Postgres，每次请求先 SELECT 再 UPDATE 那一行
把计数放在客户端本地，由前端自觉停下来不再发请求
options_en: Keep the counter in Redis, do an atomic increment-and-check, and return 429 once it trips.
Count in each instance's local memory and divide the limit by the instance count.
Store the counter in Postgres and SELECT then UPDATE the row on every request.
Keep the counter in the client and trust the frontend to stop sending.
optionExplanations: 单条 Redis 命令自带原子性，自增和判阈值不会被并发请求绕过去。
实例数随扩缩容变化，除法凑出来的限额在扩容瞬间就整体放大了。
关系库能做，但每请求一次读改写事务，限流器反而先成为瓶颈。
客户端可以被改，任何靠客户端自律的限流等于没有限流。
optionExplanations_en: A single Redis command is atomic, so increment-and-check cannot be raced past by concurrent requests.
Instance count changes with autoscaling, so a divided limit silently inflates the moment you scale out.
A relational store can do it, but a read-modify-write transaction per request makes the limiter itself the bottleneck.
Clients can be modified, so a limit enforced in the frontend is no limit at all.
why: 无状态层没有共同记忆，计数必须外置到共享存储；Redis 单命令的原子性让 incr-and-check 不会被并发放过。代价是每个请求都多一次网络往返。
why_en: A stateless tier has no shared memory, so the counter moves to Redis where a single atomic command settles increment-and-check — at the cost of one network hop per request.
tradeoff: 全局计数准确 vs 每请求多一跳 Redis
whenOtherWins: 单实例部署或允许粗糙精度时，本地内存计数更快，省掉每请求一次网络往返。

termDefinitions.meaning: 令牌桶：桶按固定速率补令牌，请求取走一个才放行，允许短时突发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token bucket refills at a fixed rate and each request consumes one token, allowing short bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定窗口：按整分钟等固定区间计数，窗口切换时计数清零。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fixed window counts requests per fixed interval and resets when the window rolls over.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次操作里先自增计数再和限额比较，避免读改写之间被并发插入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Increment-and-check raises the counter and compares it to the limit in one atomic step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限流拒绝时返回的 HTTP 状态码，表示请求太频繁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests is the status code returned when a caller is rate limited.

scenario: 每个用户有 in-flight 生成数上限，计数器放在 Redis 里；用户可能正常读完，也可能中途点了停止生成。
scenario_en: Each user has a cap on in-flight generations tracked in Redis; a run may finish normally or be cancelled midway.
q: 这个并发计数器该在哪两个时刻加减，漏掉会怎样？
q_en: When is that concurrency counter incremented and decremented, and what breaks if a step is missed?
options: 开始 incr，结束或取消 decr；漏 decr 会锁死用户
只在开始时 incr，靠 key 自然过期归零就够用了
等客户端断开 SSE 连接时才 decr，这样最省事也最准
只在生成成功完成时 decr，取消和失败的都不用管，反正很少
options_en: Increment on start, decrement on finish or cancel; a missed one locks the user out.
Only increment on start and let the key expire back to zero.
Decrement only when the client's SSE connection drops — simplest and most accurate.
Decrement only on successful completion and ignore cancels and failures since they are rare.
optionExplanations: 取消、失败、正常结束三条出口都必须落到同一个 decr 上，才对得上账。
只靠过期意味着用户在窗口内被虚高的计数误伤，配额形同随机。
断连不等于取消，后台还在生成，此时 decr 会让用户超发真实并发。
取消恰恰是最常见的出口之一，漏掉它计数只增不减，用户越用越被卡。
optionExplanations_en: All three exits — normal end, cancel, failure — must land on the same decrement for the count to balance.
Relying on expiry means an inflated count blocks the user for the rest of the window, making quotas feel random.
A dropped connection is not a cancel — generation continues, so decrementing there lets real concurrency exceed the cap.
Cancellation is one of the most common exits; skipping it makes the count only ever grow.
why: 正常路径是开始 incr、任一出口 decr；一旦取消或崩溃那条路不 decr，计数只增不减，用户到上限后每个新请求都被拒或被挂起排队，直到 TTL 兜底清理。
why_en: Increment on start and decrement on every exit; if the cancel or crash path skips it, the count only climbs until the user is rejected or queued forever, and only a TTL backstop clears it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在途：已经开始但还没结束的生成请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-flight means a generation that has started but not yet finished.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增和自减命令，用来维护共享计数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR and DECR are Redis commands that atomically raise or lower a shared counter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览器通过一条普通 HTTP 连接单向接收服务端持续推送的事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a browser receive a one-way stream of server pushes over a plain HTTP connection.

q: 把老对话续聊时 Chat Service 的上下文拼接步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put Chat Service's context carry-over steps for a follow-up turn in the right order:
scenario: 用户打开一个昨天的 chat 继续提问，模型必须表现得像还记得之前聊过什么。
scenario_en: A user reopens yesterday's chat and asks a follow-up; the model must behave as if it remembers.
steps: 按 role（user / assistant）顺序把历史消息拼成 prompt，再接上这条新消息
按 chatId 查 messages 表，按创建时间取出之前的消息
把新生成的 assistant message 写回 messages 表，供下一轮读取
把拼好的完整 prompt 发给 Inference Service
why: 模型本身不记事，"记得"完全靠每轮重新拼历史；关键是回写这一步——不写回去，下一轮就少了这次对话。代价是输入 token 随轮数一路涨。
why_en: The model itself is stateless, so memory comes from re-assembling history each turn — and the write-back is what makes the next turn complete, at the cost of input tokens growing every turn.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息的角色标记，标明这句话是 user 说的还是 assistant 说的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The role marks whether a message came from the user or the assistant.

scenario: NFR 同时要求 TTFT 低于约 500ms，以及首 token 之后这条流不出现可见空洞。
scenario_en: The NFR asks for time-to-first-token under about 500ms and no visible gaps in the stream after it.
q: 这两条要求各属于什么性质的问题，各由什么机制解决？
q_en: What kind of problem is each of these, and which mechanism solves it?
options: 前者是延迟问题→服务端推送；后者是可靠性问题→可重放的流
两条都是延迟问题，选了 SSE 一个机制就同时解决掉了
两条都是可靠性问题，靠失败后重跑整段生成来兜底
前者靠把 batch 开大解决；后者靠把轮询频率提高来解决
options_en: The first is a latency problem solved by server push; the second is a reliability problem solved by a replayable log.
Both are latency problems and picking SSE solves them together.
Both are reliability problems, handled by regenerating the whole answer on failure.
The first is fixed by a bigger batch, the second by polling more often.
optionExplanations: 一个问"第一个 token 多快到"，一个问"实例被换掉时中间那段还在不在"。
SSE 只解决推送速度，实例被替换那一瞬间丢掉的 token 它一个也补不回来。
TTFT 和失败无关，它在一切正常时也可能超标，重跑更是把延迟推得更高。
加大 batch 提升吞吐但不改善首 token；提高轮询频率只会加重浪费。
optionExplanations_en: One asks how fast the first token arrives, the other asks whether the middle survives an instance being replaced.
SSE only covers push speed; it cannot recover tokens lost while no instance was subscribed.
TTFT has nothing to do with failure — it can miss target on a perfectly healthy path, and re-running makes it worse.
A bigger batch raises throughput without helping the first token, and faster polling only wastes more requests.
why: TTFT 是纯延迟问题，靠停止轮询、一产生就推来解决；流不中断是可靠性问题，靠 runId 上一条可重放的日志解决。两套机制互不替代，混为一谈是最常见的错。
why_en: Low time-to-first-token is a pure latency problem fixed by pushing, while a gapless stream is a reliability problem fixed by a replayable per-run log — neither mechanism substitutes for the other.
tradeoff: 推送延迟 vs 断线补洞：两个目标要两套机制

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements cover system properties like latency, availability and cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户按下回车到屏幕上出现第一个 token 的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTFT is the time from hitting enter to the first token appearing on screen.

scenario: token 在某台 GPU worker 上产生，用户的连接却挂在负载均衡随手分配的任意一台无状态 Chat Service 实例上。
scenario_en: Tokens are produced on some GPU worker while the user's connection sits on whichever stateless Chat Service instance the load balancer picked.
q: 选定浏览器侧传输之后，realtime 方案还剩哪一层必须设计？
q_en: After picking the browser transport, which layer of the realtime design still has to be built?
options: 后端 fanout：把 token 送到当前持有这条连接的那台实例
客户端重排：让浏览器按序号把乱序到达的 token 拼回去
数据库分片：按 chatId 把 messages 表水平拆开
模型侧优化：换更小的模型，把首 token 的生成时间压下来
options_en: Backend fanout: getting each token to the instance currently holding this connection.
Client reordering: having the browser reassemble out-of-order tokens by sequence number.
Database sharding: splitting the messages table horizontally by chatId.
Model-side tuning: swapping in a smaller model to cut first-token latency.
optionExplanations: 生产者和持连接者是两台不同的机器，中间必须有个按 runId 会合的通道。
单条有序流不会乱序；这是多连接并发场景才需要操心的事。
分片解决的是存储容量，和把实时 token 送到正确实例毫无关系。
换小模型能压 TTFT，但 token 依然不知道该送去哪台实例。
optionExplanations_en: The producer and the connection holder are different machines, so something must let them rendezvous on the runId.
A single ordered stream does not arrive out of order; that is a multi-connection concern.
Sharding addresses storage capacity and says nothing about routing live tokens to the right instance.
A smaller model lowers TTFT but the tokens still have no way to find the right instance.
why: realtime updates 模式永远是两层：浏览器怎么收（long-polling / SSE / WebSocket），以及后端怎么把事件 fanout 到持有连接的那台实例。只做前者，一次 deploy 换掉实例流就断。
why_en: Realtime updates always has two layers — the browser transport and the backend fanout to whichever instance holds the connection — and solving only the first means a deploy kills the stream.
tradeoff: 传输层选型 vs 后端 fanout：两层各解一半，缺一不可
whenOtherWins: 如果连接和生成固定发生在同一台机器上（单机或有状态部署），fanout 这层可以省掉。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout distributes one event to every connection or subscriber that cares about it.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a full-duplex persistent connection where both sides can send at any time.

scenario: rolling summary 把较老的轮次压成一段摘要塞进 prompt，最近几轮保留逐字原文。
scenario_en: A rolling summary compresses older turns into a running summary inside the prompt while keeping the most recent turns verbatim.
q: 做摘要这件事本身要付出什么代价？
q_en: What does producing that summary itself cost?
options: 多一次更便宜的模型调用，且可能压掉后来才要紧的细节
摘要必须每一轮都重写一遍，否则内容马上就会过期
最近几轮也会一起被压缩，近期上下文同样开始失真
上下文窗口照样会被撑爆，摘要根本不解决那个硬上限
options_en: An extra, cheaper model call, plus the risk of dropping a detail that matters later.
The summary has to be rewritten every single turn or it goes stale.
Recent turns get compressed too, so nearby context also degrades.
The context window still overflows because summarizing does not move the hard ceiling.
optionExplanations: 压缩是有损的，代价既是钱（多一次调用）也是记忆保真度。
每轮重写反而会打掉 prefix 缓存，所以刻意用更慢的节奏更新。
设计恰恰相反：最近几轮留原文，被压的只有旧历史。
把旧历史压小正是让 prompt 待在窗口内的手段，说它不解决就搞反了。
optionExplanations_en: Compression is lossy, so the cost is both money for the extra call and fidelity of memory.
Rewriting each turn would invalidate the cached prefix, which is why the update runs on a slower cadence.
The design does the opposite: recent turns stay verbatim and only old history is compressed.
Shrinking old history is precisely how the prompt stays inside the window.
why: 摘要不是免费的：它是一次额外（更便宜）的模型调用，而且有损，可能丢掉几十轮后才变重要的细节。所以它要配合"只压旧上下文"的分配原则一起用。
why_en: Summarizing costs an extra cheaper model call and is lossy, so it can drop a detail that only matters much later — which is why it pairs with a rule about which context to sacrifice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 滚动摘要：把较老的对话轮次压缩成一段摘要，最近几轮保留原文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rolling summary compresses older turns into a running summary while keeping recent turns verbatim.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 prompt 中稳定不变的前缀部分的中间状态缓存起来复用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prefix caching reuses the cached model state for the stable leading part of a prompt.

scenario: 截断、摘要、按相关性检索旧事实，每种省钱手段都在拿一点答案质量换成本，而追问几乎都指向最近说过的话。
scenario_en: Truncation, summarization and relevance retrieval all trade some answer quality for cost, and follow-ups almost always point at what was just said.
q: 这份质量损失应该优先分配到哪里？
q_en: Where should that quality loss be spent first?
options: 旧的、低价值的上下文，最近几轮保持逐字原文
均匀分摊到全部历史，对每一轮都做同等力度的压缩
优先压缩最近几轮，因为它们还留在用户自己的记忆里
按 tier 分配，付费用户的对话完全不做任何压缩处理
options_en: On old, low-value context, keeping the most recent turns verbatim.
Spread evenly across all history, compressing every turn equally.
On the most recent turns, since the user still remembers those themselves.
By tier, leaving paid users' conversations entirely uncompressed.
optionExplanations: 把损失放在最不会被追问的那段，用户几乎察觉不到质量下降。
均摊会让最近几轮也开始失真，恰好命中用户最容易发现的地方。
用户记得不等于模型能引用；压掉最近几轮会立刻答非所问。
付费用户的长对话一样会撑破窗口，tier 只调阈值，不能免掉压缩。
optionExplanations_en: Spending the loss where follow-ups rarely point keeps the degradation invisible.
Spreading it evenly degrades recent turns too — exactly where users notice first.
The user remembering is not the model being able to quote it; compressing recent turns produces immediate non-sequiturs.
Long paid conversations still overflow the window; tier tunes thresholds, it cannot exempt compression.
why: 追问几乎都指向最近说过的话，所以最近几轮留原文、老历史进摘要，用户几乎感知不到。代价是极老的细节确实会丢，只能靠按相关性检索旧事实做补丁。
why_en: Follow-ups target recent turns, so keeping those verbatim and compressing old history hides the loss — at the cost of genuinely losing old details unless you retrieve them on relevance.
tradeoff: 推理成本 vs 记忆保真度：损失优先花在旧上下文
whenOtherWins: 如果任务依赖开头给出的规格（比如长文档改写），就要钉住开头而不是把它压掉。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户分层，这里指免费用户与付费用户两档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tier refers to the user class, free versus paid in this system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型一次调用能容纳的最大 token 数，超出就装不下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The context window is the maximum number of tokens one model call can hold.

scenario: prefix caching 和 rolling summary 都已经上线，长对话的推理成本还是偏高。
scenario_en: Prefix caching and rolling summaries are already in place, yet long conversations still cost too much to serve.
q: 还能叠加哪些降本杠杆？（多选）
q_en: Which additional cost levers can be stacked on top? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 只把与当前这一轮相关的旧事实检索回来，而不是整段摘要都带上
对 free tier 的超长对话设一个硬上限
把每条历史消息都写进向量库，然后全部塞回 prompt 里
把 SSE 换回轮询，用少挂几条长连接来省推理成本
options_en: Retrieve only the older facts relevant to the current turn instead of carrying the whole summary.
Put a hard cap on extremely long conversations for free-tier users.
Embed every historical message and put all of them back into the prompt.
Swap SSE back to polling and save inference cost by holding fewer long-lived connections.
optionExplanations: 按相关性挑，进 prompt 的旧内容更少，省的是每次调用的输入 token。
硬上限直接封住最贵的那条长尾，同时把成本治理接回公平性那一节。
全塞回去只会让 prompt 更大，检索的意义正是筛掉不相关的部分。
长连接开销在 Chat Service 侧，和 GPU 上的推理账单是两笔钱。
optionExplanations_en: Selecting by relevance puts less old text into the prompt, saving input tokens on every call.
A hard cap closes off the most expensive tail and ties cost control back to the fairness deep dive.
Stuffing everything back in makes the prompt larger — filtering out the irrelevant is the whole point of retrieval.
Connection overhead lives in Chat Service; the inference bill is a separate pot of money.
why: 两条杠杆都作用在同一处：让进 prompt 的旧内容更少（按相关性检索），或者干脆限制对话能长到什么程度（对 free tier 设硬上限）。后者直接接回分层公平那一节。
why_en: Both levers shrink what old context enters the prompt — retrieve only what is relevant, or cap how long a free-tier chat may grow, which loops straight back to tiered fairness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 免费用户档位，容量紧张时最先被限制或降级的一档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The free tier is the unpaid user class, first to be throttled or degraded when capacity is tight.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览器通过一条普通 HTTP 连接单向接收服务端持续推送的事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a browser receive a one-way stream of server pushes over a plain HTTP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 embedding 相似度检索文本的存储，用来找出相关的旧消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector store retrieves text by embedding similarity, used here to find relevant old messages.

tradeoff: 推理成本 vs 记忆完整度：能省的都是"少带旧内容"

scenario: 输入侧已有一个便宜分类器；输出也要审，但 token 是边生成边往用户屏幕上写的。
scenario_en: A cheap classifier already screens the prompt, but the output must be checked too — while tokens are already being written to the user's screen.
q: 输出侧审核的两难具体是什么？
q_en: What exactly is the dilemma on the output side?
options: 要么每块 flush 前先审，要么事后把消息撤回
只能等整段生成结束再审，流式体验和审核完全不可兼得
分类器必须做得和主模型一样大，否则一定会漏判
只要在输入侧拦住，输出侧就完全不需要任何检查了
options_en: Either screen each chunk before flushing it, or retract the message afterwards.
You can only screen after the whole answer finishes, so streaming and moderation cannot coexist.
The classifier must be as large as the main model or it will always miss things.
Screening the input is enough; the output needs no checking at all.
optionExplanations: 内容已经提前交付给用户了，所以只剩"先拦一下"和"事后收回"两条路。
按 chunk 审就是在保住流式的前提下审，说不可兼得等于放弃了第一条路。
输入侧用的正是便宜分类器，输出侧同理，成本约束不允许翻倍。
模型可能被绕过而生成违规内容，这正是要做输出侧那一遍的原因。
optionExplanations_en: The content has already been delivered, so only pre-flush screening or after-the-fact retraction remain.
Chunk-level screening preserves streaming, so calling them incompatible discards the first option.
The input side already uses a cheap classifier; the same cost constraint applies on the output.
A model can be talked into unsafe output, which is exactly why the second pass exists.
why: 流式把内容提前交付给了用户，所以审核要么插在每个 chunk 的 flush 之前、吃掉一点 TTFT，要么在事后把已显示的消息撤回。没有第三条路。
why_en: Streaming delivers content before it is checked, so moderation either sits in front of each chunk flush and costs latency, or pulls back a message the user has already seen.
tradeoff: 首字延迟 vs 已流出内容的可撤回性

termDefinitions.meaning: 把缓冲区里已攒好的内容真正写出到连接上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To flush is to actually write buffered content out onto the connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流式输出里一次推送出去的一小段 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chunk is one small batch of tokens pushed out at a time in a stream.

scenario: 前沿模型的权重放不进单张 GPU，必须切开摊到一整箱卡上，卡之间靠 NVLink、箱之间靠 InfiniBand 互联。
scenario_en: A frontier model's weights must be split across a whole box of GPUs, linked by NVLink inside a box and InfiniBand across boxes.
q: tensor 与 pipeline 两种并行怎么切，瓶颈落在哪？
q_en: How do tensor and pipeline parallelism split the model, and where is the bottleneck?
options: 前者切每一层，后者按层分段；互联带宽本身会成为瓶颈
前者按层分段，后者切每一层；互联带宽从来不构成瓶颈
两者都是把同一份权重复制多份，靠冗余副本提高吞吐量
两者都只影响训练，推理时模型总是完整放在单张 GPU 上
options_en: The first slices every layer, the second assigns whole layers in stages, and the interconnect itself becomes the bottleneck.
The first assigns whole layers, the second slices every layer, and the interconnect is never a bottleneck.
Both replicate the same weights and raise throughput through redundant copies.
Both matter only for training; at inference the model always fits on one GPU.
optionExplanations: 每张卡只持有权重的一部分，所以每次前向都要跨卡传数据，链路带宽直接决定上限。
方向被调换了，而且互联恰恰是这套拆分引入的新瓶颈。
复制解决的是并发副本数，解决不了"单卡装不下这份权重"这个前提。
推理同样受这个前提约束，否则整箱 GPU 的成本推导就不成立了。
optionExplanations_en: Each card holds only part of the weights, so every forward pass moves data between cards and link bandwidth sets the ceiling.
The two definitions are swapped, and the interconnect is precisely the new bottleneck this split introduces.
Replication adds concurrent copies but does nothing about weights not fitting on one card.
Inference faces the same constraint, which is what the whole box-of-GPUs cost estimate rests on.
why: tensor parallelism 让每张卡持有每层的一片，pipeline parallelism 让每张卡持有整层并往下传；两种切法都把计算变成跨卡通信，NVLink / InfiniBand 的带宽因此成为新瓶颈。
why_en: Tensor parallelism gives each GPU a slice of every layer while pipeline parallelism gives it whole layers to hand onward, and either way compute turns into cross-device traffic bounded by NVLink and InfiniBand.
tradeoff: 两种切分方式不同，但都换来对互联带宽的依赖

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每一层的权重横向切片分给多张 GPU，每次前向都要跨卡合并结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tensor parallelism slices each layer across GPUs, so every forward pass merges partial results across devices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同的层分给不同 GPU，数据像流水线一样一段段往下传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pipeline parallelism assigns different layers to different GPUs and passes activations down the line.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一台机器内 GPU 之间的高速互联链路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NVLink is the high-speed interconnect between GPUs inside one machine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器之间的高速网络互联，用于跨箱连接 GPU 集群。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InfiniBand is the high-speed network fabric linking GPU machines to each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器，这里指跑大模型推理的加速卡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU is the accelerator card that runs large-model inference here.
